items.title: OpenRouter 教程：用 LLM 从 PDF 中抽取表格
items.description: OpenRouter 发布教程，讲解如何把 PDF 以文件形式连同严格 JSON schema 发给能读文件的模型，让表格以带类型的行返回，括号亏损、千分位和脚注标记等清理都写进字段描述。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/l928e49lwysm0ymgmhyjrkc3z
items.excerpt:
How to Extract Tables from a PDF with an LLM
OpenRouter 发布教程，讲解如何把 PDF 以文件形式连同严格 JSON schema 发给能读文件的模型，让表格以带类型的行返回，括号亏损、千分位和脚注标记等清理都写进字段描述。
OpenRouter 用五份 PDF 实测了多条抽取路由，给出严格 JSON schema 写法、两类静默失败的检查和各路由成本对比。
要用 LLM 从 PDF 中提取表格，请将 PDF 发送给 能够读取文件的模型 ，同时提供一个 严格的 JSON schema ，用于描述表格中的一行。模型会返回带类型的行。数量会以整数返回，写成 (3,878) 的亏损会返回为 -3878，跨两页的表格会返回为一个列表。
我们在五个 PDF 上测试了这一点，其中两个是扫描件。每个直接读取 PDF 的模型都答对了全部 644 个单元格。我们测试中的失败来自 PDF 到达模型所经过的路径，其中两次返回了正常响应且没有报错。
代码适用于数字 PDF 和扫描件，但结果取决于 PDF 是否有文本层、扫描质量、解析器路径和模型。示例使用了五个测试 PDF，它们由已知数据生成，因此每个单元格都可以与源数据核对。它们分别是一张发票、一份季度报告、一份跨到第二页的 58 行发货日志、一份扫描的采购订单，以及一份故意做得很粗糙、带有合并单元格的扫描件。
将以下内容保存为 extract_tables.py 。它会将 PDF 作为文件内容部分发送，如我们的 PDF 输入 页面所述，并通过 结构化输出 请求与你的 schema 匹配的 JSON。将 strict 设为 true 时，支持严格模式的提供商会让输出符合 schema，因此每一行都有每个字段且类型正确。支持情况因提供商而异，结构化输出页面展示了如何仅路由到支持它的提供商。
return 之前的两个检查会捕获第 3 步和第 4 步中涵盖的失败，因此请保留它们。成本来自 usage.cost ， 用量统计 会在每个响应中包含它。
该调用耗时约六秒。PDF 显示 6,067.00，而行中保存的是 6067.0，这是一个无需先清理就能相加的数字。字段描述移除了千位分隔符。
PDF 表格所需的大部分清理工作都可以放入 schema 的字段描述中。我们的季度报告有一个跨四个季度列的“Fiscal 2026”表头，亏损写在括号中，并且两个分部名称（Enterprise 和 Hardware resale）上有脚注标记。字段描述处理括号和脚注标记。跨列表头不需要描述，因为字段名已经说明了每个值属于哪个季度。
在 Hardware resale 这一行中，(3,878) 返回成了 -3878，而且两个片段名称里的脚注标记都不见了。
沿列向下合并的单元格也是同样的道理。在我们的粗略扫描中，每个 Category 单元格跨六到九行。我们把这个字段描述为“第一列中的类别。它是合并单元格，因此要在它覆盖的每一行上重复。”在我们的测试中，这足以让三个能读取 PDF 的模型都在全部 30 行上填入类别。
如果模型能读取文件，我们就把 PDF 直接传给它。如果模型不能读取文件，我们先解析 PDF，再把结果发给模型。文件解析器插件的 engine 设置决定使用哪个解析器。当你在一个不能读取文件的模型上不设置它时，我们会使用 mistral-ocr ，正如 PDF 输入 页面所述。根据你的 PDF 长什么样来选择路线。
下面是把扫描的采购订单分别用每种解析器发送给 deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash 的结果。该模型接受图像但不接受文件，所以 PDF 必须经过解析器。
那个 ValueError 来自第 1 步中的空行检查。如果没有该检查，第二次调用会返回 200 OK，并带有 finish_reason: "stop" 和 {"rows": []} 。解析器在扫描件上找不到文本，模型也正确地报告了空表格。没有任何东西抛出错误，所以没有该检查的流水线会存储零行，然后继续处理下一个文件。这是两个静默失败中的第一个。我们的粗略扫描表现相同，30 行中得了 0 分。
原生引擎只适用于能读取文件的模型。当我们还是在 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 上设置 engine="native" 时，请求成功了一次，然后两次因提供商错误而失败。
在同一个模型上不设置 engine 时，我们试了两次都成功了，所以不要在不能读取文件的模型上设置 native 。
模型写出的每一行都会消耗输出 token，所以长表格需要较高的 max_tokens 。我们那份 58 行的发货日志根据模型不同使用了 2,500 到 7,700 个输出 token，这让最啰嗦的模型在 extract_table 中默认的 8,000 之下几乎没有余量。算下来每行是 43 到 133 个 token。对于长表格，从每个预期行约 150 个 token 开始。然后测量你自己的行，并保留 finish_reason 检查，因为计数会因模型和 schema 而异。下面是限制太低时会发生的情况。
如果没有 finish_reason 检查，这个请求会以两种方式之一失败。普通 JSON 解析会在被截断的数组上抛出错误。
第二种方式是另一个静默失败。开启 Response Healing 插件后，JSON 能解析，你会得到 58 行中的 5 行，且没有异常。Healing 会修复输出的语法，其文档警告说它无法恢复被 max_tokens 截断的输出，所以它无法添加模型从未写出的行。 finish_reason 检查能捕获这两种情况。
每一行都有 schema 中定义的键，因此 csv.DictWriter 可以从 schema 中获取列名，并按原样写入各行。Excel 可以直接打开结果。
表格延伸到了第二页，并在那里重复了表头。CSV 只有一个表头，包含全部 58 行。

items.excerpt:
In general, LLM performance is incredibly multidimensional. There's no guarantee of a fixed ordering where the model that is best at math is also the model that's best at jokes. Despite that complexity, much of the variation in performance is explained by just a single variable: model size. In general, models that are bigger will (a) be more performant / reliable, (b) cost more per token, and (c) have better recall of esoteric facts. As you note, our models are ordered:
[ ... ] These days, version number signifies a few things at once: the order of release, the relationship to other releases, and the magnitude of improvement. So something like 6.1 would indicate it was launched after 5.6, may share some similarities to other 6.1 models in terms of training data / personality (which is why it's not 5.7), and isn't a giant enough leap to merit the headlines and expectations that would come with a 7.
— Ted Sanders , explaining OpenAI's model naming conventions
This is a quotation collected by Simon Willison, posted on 28th October 2026 .

items.title: Anthropic 报告：Claude 研究模型在 Chrome、Safari、Android、Windows、Linux 发现漏洞并串联 5 条攻击链
items.description: Anthropic 于 10 月 27 日发布研究报告，称一个未公开的内部 Claude 研究模型在 Chrome、Safari、Android、Windows 和 Linux 中发现漏洞，串联出 5 条可实际运行的攻击链，相关漏洞已按协调披露流程报告并修复。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/jpt1eeuj2p1mgrxbufuv3ntdn
items.excerpt:
Claude AI 找漏洞实战：安卓手机锁屏下提取照片、53 分钟攻破 Linux 获取最高权限
Anthropic 于 10 月 27 日发布研究报告，称一个未公开的内部 Claude 研究模型在 Chrome、Safari、Android、Windows 和 Linux 中发现漏洞，串联出 5 条可实际运行的攻击链，相关漏洞已按协调披露流程报告并修复。
原文梳理了五条攻击链的关键数字和影响范围，读者可据此评估 AI 自主挖掘漏洞的实际能力边界。
IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，Anthropic 于 10 月 27 日发布研究报告，称其通过一个未公开发布的内部 Claude 研究模型，在 Chrome、Safari、 Android 、Windows 和 Linux 中发现漏洞， 并将多个漏洞串联为 5 条可实际运行的攻击链。相关漏洞均已按协调披露流程报告厂商并修复。
其中最受关注的是 Chrome，IT之家援引博文介绍，Anthropic 向谷歌提交的报告共产生 62 个严重或高危 CVE，包括 13 个沙箱逃逸漏洞和 21 个可控制网页渲染进程的漏洞，修复已随 Chrome 156 发布。
研究团队称，Claude 在研究人员给出初始提示后，自主定位漏洞并编写利用代码；其 Chrome 概念验证可在页面加载后数秒内于 macOS 默认安装环境中打开计算器应用。
Safari 方面，Claude 发现的漏洞链可绕过同源策略，让恶意网站有机会读取用户已登录账号的数据；苹果已在同日确认并发布修复。Android 攻击则需物理接触设备，可在 Pixel 9 锁屏状态下通过 USB 提取照片等个人数据，谷歌称已处理该问题。
在 Windows 方面，Claude 重点发现追踪编号为 CVE-2026-33096 的漏洞，评分为 7.5，攻击者无需认证或用户交互即可让响应 HTTP/3 请求的服务器崩溃；微软已于 2026 年 4 月发布补丁。
最严重的是 Linux 漏洞 CVE-2026-98432，这是针对运行多路径 TCP 监听器的服务器，攻击者发送数据包即可在无凭据情况下获得 root shell。Anthropic 的验证共耗时 53 分钟，其中 48 分钟用于泄露内核指针，5 分钟执行命令。
Anthropic 公布了 5 条串联多个漏洞、配置弱点或竞态条件，最终实现数据窃取、系统崩溃或远程控制等 5 条攻击链：
攻击从 V8 JavaScript 引擎漏洞开始，随后绕过 Chrome 的内存沙箱，再利用 CacheStorage 竞态条件和 FedCM 的释放后使用缺陷，最终在沙箱外执行任意代码。
模型构建了一条“一次点击”攻击链，绕过同源策略，让恶意网页访问本应隔离的其他网站数据，可读取浏览器历史、Cookie 及登录状态下的邮件、银行等敏感信息。
该链条针对被锁定或未解锁的 Pixel 9 安卓 手机，利用 USB 相关缺陷，在设备未解锁时提取照片等个人信息。手机即使处于锁屏状态，仍可能泄露本地媒体与个人资料。
Claude 发现 Windows QUIC 内核实现中的越界读取漏洞，可远程触发服务器反复崩溃。
研究团队称，Claude 在 Linux 内核网络栈中发现一个零点击远程代码执行漏洞，可在约 53 分钟内获得 root 权限。
原文梳理了五条攻击链的关键数字和影响范围，读者可据此评估 AI 自主挖掘漏洞的实际能力边界。

items.title: Kardex AI-powered BinInductAI makes AutoStore faster and more accurate
items.description: Kardex’s new BinInductAI intelligent bin induction innovation uses vision and AI-based image analysis to improve quality control. The post Kardex AI-powered BinInductAI makes AutoStore faster and more accurate appeared first on Automated Warehouse .
items.excerpt:
Kardex has launched BinInductAI, an artificial intelligence and computer vision-driven system designed to streamline the AutoStore bin induction process by eliminating manual pre-checks and scanning, ultimately cutting on-site induction time by up to 30%.
The company said its innovations in BinInductAI are intended to enhance performance and efficiency across the system lifecycle – from implementation and orchestration to picking , maintenance, and inventory validation.
The Kardex Intuitive Picking Assistant (IPA) projects all relevant picking information onto the AutoStore port to enhance throughput, reduce errors, and improve inventory control, while the recently launched PortScale precision weighing system double-checks accuracy.
The net result is a reduction in manual effort and improved accuracy while unlocking greater value from the automated storage and retrieval system ( ASRS ), asserted Kardex.
The use of computer vision and AI-based image analysis simplifies the induction process, Kardex said.
Operators simply place the bin in the induction port, with no manual scanning or pre-checks required, it explained. Before induction, the system automatically performs a series of quality checks, verifying and inspecting bin presence, bin walls, robot pickup holes, and barcode readability.
Once the barcode is validated, BinInductAI confirms with the ASRS that the bin is not already registered to prevent duplicates before automatically sending the insertion commands and inducting the bin into the AutoStore grid.
Submit your innovation now! Reducing risk during bin induction BinInductAI standardizes verification for every bin, ensuring that quality checks are thorough and consistent, said Kardex.
Before a bin enters the system , BinInductAI automatically identifies damaged or out-of-spec bins, preventing potential problems from affecting the AutoStore grid and reducing the risk of downstream disruptions. By automating what has traditionally been a manual process, the solution reduces operator workload and minimizes the potential for human error during implementation, the company said.
The result is a more reliable and efficient induction process that helps improve system readiness and supports smoother AutoStore implementation, particularly during critical go-live and startup phases, claimed Kardex. items.title: Symbotic partnership with Walmart offers robotics lessons about anchor customers
items.description: The growing Symbotic partnership with Walmart shows how an anchor customer can help a startup’s scale but also creates risks. The post Symbotic partnership with Walmart offers robotics lessons about anchor customers appeared first on Automated Warehouse .
items.excerpt:
Symbotic Inc.’s recent quarterly filing lists its largest customer, together with affiliates, as “Customer A,” and its annual report named that customer as Walmart. Customer A supplied 90.5% of revenue in the quarter that ended June 27, 2026. Symbotic reported $720.8 million in revenue and $55 million in net income for the same quarter.
Few robotics companies have turned one demanding customer into a business this size, and this profit follows earlier profits . The quarter also included $19.4 million of investment gains and negative non-GAAP free cash flow, so one quarter’s profit can’t settle whether leaning so heavily on Walmart has paid off.
For a startup founder deciding whether to sign a second customer soon, Walmart’s 90.5% share says little about the cost of serving another account. I’d look at how many people that account pulls into the field and what the contract obliges each side to do when plans change. I’d also ask how easily the anchor could get the same work done another way.
Symbotic can’t afford to lose Walmart, and that dependence already gives the retailer some protection. Walmart’s contracts show that it didn’t rely on that incentive alone. The 2022 master automation agreement gives Walmart continuity rights, including the right to embed engineers with Symbotic and technical material held in escrow, which Walmart can use under specified conditions.
The 2025 agreement for Walmart’s store-level Accelerated Pickup and Delivery (APD) systems repeats those protections. During the APD build-out, it also caps, at a redacted number, how many comparable APD systems Symbotic can sell to each outside customer every year. The filings don’t show whether Walmart has ever tested these rights, so they read more like preparation than a proven fallback.
When the APD deal closed in January 2025, Walmart committed $520 million of development funding. Symbotic paid Walmart a $200 million base price for its robotics business in the same transaction and agreed to two possible milestone payments of $175 million each.
Symbotic gained funded development and the prospect of a large rollout, although the additional purchase commitment depends on performance milestones. In return, the Wilmington, Mass.-based company accepted delivery obligations and limits on comparable APD sales to other customers.

items.title: Why Agents Love Supabase
items.description: Paul Copplestone and Ant Wilson on building the backend for AI agents
items.excerpt:
Paul Copplestone and Ant Wilson on building the backend for AI agents
I first met Paul Copplestone and Ant Wilson in Singapore, shortly after they finished YC as the hottest startup of YC S20 . Six years later, we finally got them on the podcast! This is their first podcast together, after taking an open-source, fully remote company from zero to a $10 billion valuation.
The title is a question I wanted to understand for myself: why do agents love Supabase? There are plenty of managed databases. Postgres hosting is competitive. Being familiar to a model is useful distribution, but it doesn't explain all the work needed to turn a generated application into something that runs. But when I ran my frontier AEO tracker , it was an almost complete sweep of first choice for app backends (and in contention for managed db ) for every frontier model from Astra to Fable to Muse.
At Select, Supabase grouped its announcements into Build, Operate and Scale.
The things that stood out to me were surprisingly practical: start a local backend without Docker, keep the desired database schema in Git, and run compute beside the database. Each removes a piece of work that developers have been doing for years. Agents make that friction harder to ignore.
Watch the full conversation, including my opening commentary →
My favorite developer-tool announcements make me think: of course I want this today. The new alpha runtime for running Supabase locally without Docker is one of those. I use Colima rather than Docker Desktop, and even then, removing another dependency from the path to a working database is welcome. Local setup is a small part of a human developer's week; an agent that repeatedly creates and tests environments encounters it over and over.
Declarative schemas are the bigger idea. The familiar SQL workflow accumulates a history: create the schema, then migrate, migrate, migrate. A declarative representation gives the agent a description of the state you want, in files it can inspect and edit alongside the application.
In the commentary, I compare this to a Terraform moment for the database. Put the desired state in Git and the agent can read it, change it, fork it and work against it as part of the repository. Humans get the same advantage: the backend becomes easier to understand without reconstructing its entire history.

items.title: Interview with Faraday Future chairman: Moving from Chinese robot sourcing to US manufacturing
items.description: Faraday Future is best known as an electric vehicle company, but it is increasingly positioning robotics as a major part of its future, describing itself more broadly as a “physical AI ecosystem company”. The California-based company is now trying to build a US robotics business around technology and products that currently rely substantially on Chinese […]
items.excerpt:
Faraday Future is best known as an electric vehicle company, but it is increasingly positioning robotics as a major part of its future, describing itself more broadly as a “physical AI ecosystem company”.
The California-based company is now trying to build a US robotics business around technology and products that currently rely substantially on Chinese manufacturing partners.
At its recent “Built in USA” conference in Los Angeles, FF outlined plans to bring a US robot factory online by the end of 2026, with its first US-assembled robot scheduled for February 2027.
The company ultimately wants to move beyond domestic assembly towards greater US manufacturing, while introducing three to five new or next-generation robotics products in the country each year.
That strategy comes at an interesting time. Chinese manufacturers have established a commanding position in the rapidly growing humanoid robotics market, while US regulators are paying increasing attention to foreign-made connected technologies and their supply chains.
For FF, therefore, bringing robotics production to the US is about more than simply moving an assembly line. The company sees localization as a way to strengthen regulatory compliance, supply-chain resilience, quality control and customer support while gradually developing domestic suppliers and manufacturing capabilities.
In this interview with Robotics & Automation News , Jerry Wang , global executive chairman of Faraday Future, explains how the company intends to make that transition and why it believes its experience in electric vehicles gives it a useful starting point.
Wang discusses the implications of new FCC rules, the likely cost disadvantage of manufacturing robots in the US and the challenges involved in replacing imported components with domestically sourced alternatives.
He also explains how FF could reuse parts of its existing EV manufacturing infrastructure, including its Hanford, California factory, and argues that electric vehicles and robots are not simply two unrelated businesses.
Instead, Wang says technologies including AI, perception, sensor fusion, computing, connectivity and data can form a common foundation for both – with robotics potentially becoming a significant new growth business alongside FF’s automotive operations.
Robotics & Automation News : What specifically do the new FCC rules change for Faraday Future and other US companies currently sourcing robotics products from overseas manufacturers?
Jerry Wang

Neura Robotics and the Technical University of Munich have opened a €17 million robotics research and training center near Munich Airport, while unveiling the latest generation of Neura’s 4NE1 humanoid robot.
The TUM RoboGym powered by Neura covers more than 2,300 square meters at LabCampus and combines robotics research, training and industrial applications.
Built in partnership with TUM’s Munich Institute of Robotics and Machine Intelligence (MIRMI), the facility enables companies to bring real industrial tasks into a research environment where robots can learn and test new skills.
Companies from more than ten industries are already involved, including automotive, pharmaceuticals, medical technology, packaging, logistics, agriculture and care.
Tasks being trained include handling cardboard boxes, filling bottles and loading and unloading wooden components.
David Reger, founder and CEO of Neura Robotics, said: “Our companies hold knowledge that has been built up over generations. People know how to work materials, assemble components and master difficult processes.

“With the launch of the humanoid 4NE1 Gen 4, we are showing today which robots are ready for it: designed for series production, built for productive work and powered by Neuron AI, our own foundation model that learns from experience in the NEURA Gyms. Developed, built and trained in Germany, for the world.”
The RoboGym combines three approaches to generating physical AI training data: real-world robot operation, human demonstrations and simulation.
Human workflows can be captured using sensor-equipped data suits, motion capture and teleoperation, while virtual environments provide additional variations that can subsequently be validated using physical robots.
Neura’s Neuraverse connects the training infrastructure with the company’s software and AI tools.

items.title: Maxinsights raises $30 million to build training data platform for physical AI
items.description: Maxinsights has raised $30 million in seed funding to expand its physical AI data platform, which pays people to record everyday activities such as cooking, cleaning and other work to generate training data for robots and AI models. The company was founded by robotics and autonomous-driving veterans, with its wider engineering team including former employees […]
items.excerpt:
Maxinsights has raised $30 million in seed funding to expand its physical AI data platform, which pays people to record everyday activities such as cooking, cleaning and other work to generate training data for robots and AI models.
The company was founded by robotics and autonomous-driving veterans, with its wider engineering team including former employees of Waymo, Google, Microsoft and Meta.
The funding round was led by PeakXV, with participation from Tola Capital, South Park Commons, INCE Capital and Alumni Ventures.
Maxinsights has also launched MaxLoop, an AI-based system for monitoring and improving the quality of collected footage, and MaxGlove, a sensor glove designed to capture tactile information such as grip force and object weight that cannot be obtained from video alone.
The company says it has captured more than 2 million hours of real-world human activity, of which 1.5 million hours is model-ready, and serves more than 30 customers, including AI labs and foundation model developers.
More than 5,000 contractors across six countries use Maxinsights’ camera hardware to record themselves carrying out everyday activities, ranging from loading dishwashers and preparing food to washing cars.
Unlike staged data collection, the approach is intended to expose AI models to the variation and unexpected events encountered in real homes and workplaces.
Yuguang (YG) Yuan, founder and CEO of Maxinsights, said: “We built the whole pipeline ourselves, from the hand-tracking models to the platform that scores every operator’s footage as it arrives, because nobody was going to sell us the pieces that make messy real-world data usable.
“Robots get deployed into real kitchens, not staged ones, and something unexpected happens every few minutes. Edge cases are the job, and the only way to get them is to record real work in real homes. Collecting one great hour of data is easy, and holding quality across millions of hours and thousands of people is what we built the company to do.”
MaxLoop automatically assesses incoming footage and provides feedback to operators. Maxinsights says the system has reduced review costs by approximately 80 percent and enables it to process 450,000 hours of footage a month.
MaxGlove, meanwhile, is being developed with Genesis AI to capture force and touch information, including pressure, resistance and slip.
Maxinsights is targeting 1 million hours of force data in 2027 using the glove and its existing collection network.

items.title: What Symbotic’s Walmart growth teaches robotics startups about anchor customers
items.description: Symbotic’s growth with Walmart shows how an anchor customer can fund a robotics startup’s scale while creating risks around customer concentration, contractual restrictions and the challenge of building a diversified, repeatable business. The post What Symbotic’s Walmart growth teaches robotics startups about anchor customers appeared first on The Robot Report .
items.excerpt:
Symbotic’s recent quarterly filing lists its largest customer, together with affiliates, as “Customer A,” and the annual report names that customer as Walmart. Customer A supplied 90.5% of revenue in the quarter that ended June 27, 2026. Symbotic reported $720.8 million in revenue and $55 million in net income for the same quarter.
Few robotics companies have turned one demanding customer into a business this size, and this profit follows earlier profits . The quarter also included $19.4 million of investment gains and negative non-GAAP free cash flow, so one quarter’s profit can’t settle whether leaning so heavily on Walmart has paid off.
For a startup founder deciding whether to sign a second customer soon, Walmart’s 90.5% share says little about the cost of serving another account. I’d look at how many people that account pulls into the field and what the contract obliges each side to do when plans change. I’d also ask how easily the anchor could get the same work done another way.
Symbotic can’t afford to lose Walmart, and that dependence already gives the retailer some protection. Walmart’s contracts show that it didn’t rely on that incentive alone. The 2022 master automation agreement gives Walmart continuity rights, including the right to embed engineers with Symbotic and technical material held in escrow, which Walmart can use under specified conditions. The 2025 agreement for Walmart’s store-level Accelerated Pickup and Delivery (APD) systems repeats those protections. During the APD build-out, it also caps, at a redacted number, how many comparable APD systems Symbotic can sell to each outside customer every year. The filings don’t show whether Walmart has ever tested these rights, so they read more like preparation than a proven fallback.
When the APD deal closed in January 2025, Walmart committed $520 million of development funding. Symbotic paid Walmart a $200 million base price for its robotics business in the same transaction and agreed to two possible milestone payments of $175 million each. Symbotic gained funded development and the prospect of a large rollout, although the additional purchase commitment depends on performance milestones. In return, it accepted delivery obligations and limits on comparable APD sales to other customers.

items.excerpt:
German firm NAiSE provides a single software layer to control AGVs and AMRs from different vendors.
The supply chain technology company Körber is acquiring a stake in NAiSE GmbH, a Germany-based software company specializing in vendor-agnostic fleet management, saying the two partners will now combine their capabilities to enable customers to orchestrate mixed vehicle fleets across production and warehouse environments.
Founded in 2017, NAiSE says its fleet management software (FMS) brings together automated guided vehicles (AGVs) and autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) from different vendors and manually operated industrial trucks on a shared control layer, regardless of which Warehouse Management System (WMS), Warehouse Execution System (WES), or Warehouse Control System (WCS) is running in the background. That capability has become more important as companies are increasingly relying on larger vehicle fleets from different vendors. Without a higher-level control layer, such fleets remain isolated stand-alone solutions, limiting their efficiency, transparency, and scalability.
Together, NAiSE and Körber also intend to develop new use cases for intralogistics applications, including humanoid robotics.
“With NAiSE, we are gaining a partner that addresses the orchestration of mixed fleets with an approach that is vendor-agnostic, standardized, and field-proven, exactly what the market needs today. Together with the founding team, we will unlock this potential and offer our customers an end-to-end automation solution,” said Helena Garriga, Körber Executive Board Member and responsible for the Business Area Supply Chain.
Details of the investment were not disclosed, but the companies said that NAiSE will continue its business with existing and new partners unchanged. Operational management of the company will remain with the founding team of Kai Przybysz-Herz, Robert Libert, and Raphael Kusumoto. And Körber will act as a strategic investor and sparring partner, supporting NAiSE in its next phase of growth.

items.title: The Payroll Challenges of Scaling Robotics Businesses
items.description: Robotics companies are continuously expanding into new markets. As a result, many businesses are setting up offices in multiple countries or hiring remote international workers to accommodate their growth. While this is helping robotics businesses scale their operations, it does come with its fair share of challenges. One of the biggest is managing payroll. So, […]
items.excerpt:
Robotics companies are continuously expanding into new markets. As a result, many businesses are setting up offices in multiple countries or hiring remote international workers to accommodate their growth.
While this is helping robotics businesses scale their operations, it does come with its fair share of challenges. One of the biggest is managing payroll.
So, with that in mind, let’s take a look at how paying permanent staff, contractors, and project-based workers across multiple locations can be challenging for a business, and what robotics companies are doing to manage these obstacles effectively.
For businesses with international staff, keeping on top of different tax rules, reporting requirements, and labour laws can be a real challenge.
Each country has its own tax rates, contribution requirements, and reporting criteria, so maintaining compliance and accurately calculating wages and contributions is far from straightforward.
Many robotics companies rely on a mix of permanent and temporary staff, contractors, and project-based workers, which can lead to complex payroll requirements. As an example, in the UK permanent staff are paid on a regular schedule through PAYE, whereas contractors are paid daily or by the hour and their taxes are handled by the individual or a third-party umbrella or limited company.
Another major complication is exchange rates. These fluctuate a lot and it can have an impact on the cost of payroll month-to-month and alter an employee’s expected take-home pay.
Of course, all the additional challenges of international payroll creates a huge amount of admit for HR and finance teams, and this can have a knock on effect. Being bogged down by admin leaves these departments with little time to focus on the projects that keep a business moving forward.
Sending money across the border can take a considerable amount of time depending on the bank and the country. Additionally, this may incur extra fees for the business, increasing payroll-related outgoings.
One of the most common methods to manage global employees is by using an international payroll service. These systems help simplify payments and maintain compliance by handling local tax brackets, contributions, and deductions automatically, paying workers in their local currencies, and offering multi-system integrations to keep all employee data and information in one place.

items.title: The Factory PCs Nobody Patches: Why Automation Needs Remote Monitoring
items.description: By Nathan Spitalny, CEO of RDE Technologies Walk through most small and mid-sized plants and you’ll find them: the Windows box running the HMI on line two, the SCADA workstation in the control room, the engineering laptop that only comes out when a PLC program needs changing. They keep production moving, and they are often […]
items.excerpt:
By Nathan Spitalny , CEO of RDE Technologies
Walk through most small and mid-sized plants and you’ll find them: the Windows box running the HMI on line two, the SCADA workstation in the control room, the engineering laptop that only comes out when a PLC program needs changing. They keep production moving, and they are often the least-watched computers in the building.
Office IT usually gets the attention. Laptops are patched, email is filtered, and someone is alerted when a server fills up. The plant-floor PCs are different. They were set up by an integrator, they “just work,” and nobody wants to touch them in case a reboot stops a line.
Remote monitoring and management, or RMM software , puts a small agent on each Windows machine and reports its health to one dashboard.
For plant-floor PCs, the useful checks are basic:
The key is configuration. On production machines, patching should be approved and timed around maintenance windows, and alerts should go to someone who understands that rebooting an HMI mid-shift is not an option.
RMM tools are powerful, and attackers know it. In 2023, CISA warned that criminals were using legitimate remote monitoring tools to gain access and avoid detection ( CISA advisory AA23-025A ).
So treat the RMM console like the keys to the plant: require multi-factor authentication, limit who can open remote sessions, log every session, and keep the agent off PLCs and safety systems entirely. RMM belongs on the Windows machines, not on the controllers themselves.
Begin with an inventory: list every Windows machine that touches production, its operating system and who supports it. Then put the most critical few under monitoring, agree patch windows with operations, and separate the plant network from the office.
None of this needs new robots or a big budget. It just means treating the computers behind automation with the same care as the ones on desks.
About the author : Nathan Spitalny is the CEO of RDE Technologies , a managed IT and cybersecurity provider founded in 2009 in Oceanside, New York. His team supports healthcare practices, senior-living facilities and small businesses across New York City and Long Island.

items.excerpt:
Ed Zitron 撰文批评 Anthropic 的 S-1 招股书，指其仅披露 Q2 盈利数据、省略 Q3 现金状况和付款明细，是在公司基本面变化前误导投资者。
作者基于 Anthropic S-1 逐项拆解其逾 4300 亿美元不可撤销算力承诺与收入结构风险，可用于对照招股书原文核实。
我打算暂停一周的付费内容，因为这周家里有事占去了我大量时间，不过下周五（11/6）我会带着一篇重磅内容回归。
在此期间，我正在进行为期一周的促销活动——新订阅用户可享受每年70美元订阅费 终身 九折优惠（ 点击这里！ ）。这是支持我工作的绝佳方式，而且你能以低于几乎所有竞品简报的价格获得极其丰富的价值。
过去几个月里，我发表了关于AI债务世界的 两 部分 指南、一篇关于 生成式AI对全球经济（可疑）影响 的分析、对AI基础设施领域最大参与者的深度分析，比如NVIDIA（ 上 篇和 下 篇）和Oracle（ 上 篇和 下 篇）、 OpenAI最终将如何杀死Oracle ，以及 风险投资如何杀死自己 。
如果你想联系我——尤其是如果你掌握关于Anthropic、OpenAI、Blackstone或AI泡沫中任何其他公司的劲爆信息——请通过Signal联系我，号码是ezitron.76。你也可以在你的Bloomberg Terminal上通过IB找到我。
上周 ，我在简报开头引用了Apollo首席经济学家Torsten Slok的一句话，请原谅， 我不得不再引用一次 ，重点是他 本人 强调的：
从大局来看，AI的整个卖点在于它是一种 增强器 或 岗位替代器 ，我的意思是它能让 你当前的资源更高效和/或更具生产力 ，或者 让你能够替代上述资源 ，这里的“资源”指的是现金、人员、软件或其他你用来经营业务的东西。
我之所以用这么费雪牌（Fisher Price）式的说法，是因为AI泡沫是通过刻意回避你用来衡量企业健康状况的术语而被吹大的。泡沫已经四年了，AI至少理论上应该对商业世界 做点什么 ——某种 可衡量的 事情，尤其是几乎所有人都在谈论要在各处部署它、一直使用它。
然而自AI泡沫开始以来，标普500的利润率似乎变得 更糟 了，ChatGPT在2022年11月的发布似乎对那些不叫Google、Amazon、Meta、Microsoft或NVIDIA的公司 屁用没有 ，而Tesla和Apple与我们理解的AI泡沫关系甚微。
AI 吹捧者和不满者花了将近四年的时间，试图让所有人去谈论任何可以想象到的统计数据， 唯独 不谈那些真正重要的数据，主要是因为这些数据无一例外都长 这样 ：
他们将要给出的反驳是“各组织尚未将 AI 完全安装到其工作流程中”之类的商业说辞，与其说是 移动球门柱 ，不如说是 不断改变游戏规则，以至于我们都搞不清自己到底在玩什么。 它并没有让公司赚更多的钱、获得更多利润，也没有以现代科学可以衡量的方式改善它们。
而且， 根据 Slok 上周的说法 ，它甚至没有提高超大规模云服务商的 ROIC（投入资本回报率），而这还是在 Meta 宣布计划通过持续股权销售筹集近 1000 亿美元 之前：
看来 AI 似乎并没有在标普 500 指数成分股中带来收入或利润率的增长，除了那七家巨头之外——而它们以超过一万亿美元的资本支出为代价，换来的却是投入资本回报率逐季 下降 。
然而，每一家构建任何与 AI 相关产品的公司都会告诉你，它正在 改变一切 ，而且 你今天就必须加入 ，即使产品并不像他们说的那样真正有效，即使并没有真正 tangible 的证据表明这是一笔好投资，即使很明显运营这些服务的公司有着极其可疑的经济账。
引用经济学家 Paul Kedrosky 在 Prof G Markets 播客上的话 ：“……这份 [S-1] 从当前业务结构的角度来看已经好得不能再好了。而现在你要经历这个拐点，这会让它变得资本密集得多。”
我要说得更狠一点，因为我认为 Anthropic 正在以 IPO 史上前所未见的规模故意误导投资者。任何人对现金流或对“盈利能力”的宽松定义可能抱有的兴奋都无关紧要，因为 Anthropic 按其自己的承认及其令人难以置信的义务来看，已经是一家与今年第二季度时完全不同的公司。
所以，正如你可能已经读到的， Anthropic 终于在本周早些时候发布了其 S-1 ，这是一份 300 多页的庞然大物，包含各种风险因素和披露信息，同时也小心翼翼地避开了可能有助于全面分析它的内容，特别是 略去了任何与其第三季度数据相关的内容 ，而这些数据是在其投资者日期间披露的。
尽管有种种喧嚣和盲目乐观的自我安慰，绝大多数数字其实早已为人所知，而许多新数字让情况变得难上加难。
这意味着我们掌握的最新季度——2026 年第二季度——是“盈利”的（ 正如我在 5 月所讨论的 ），原因是 SpaceX 在该季度三个月中的两个月给予了折扣：
因此，Anthropic 的盈利季度——具体来说是 9.74 亿美元的利润——在很大程度上是由很可能永远不会再发生的事件造成的。
事实上，未来几个季度将发生 截然相反 的情况，因为无论公司表现如何，Anthropic 庞大的不可取消负担都将开始拖累其资产负债表。
你看，这是一份 择机而发 的 S-1，因为 Anthropic 的大部分大型算力合同都是在 2026 年第二季度或前后才启动的，其中与亚马逊和谷歌签订的 2245 亿美元不可取消协议分别于 4 月和 5 月开始。
就 SpaceX 而言，算力账单比我们想象的要大得多，从 此前报道的每月 12.5 亿美元 ，到 2026 年 12 月已增至每月 31 亿美元，约合每年 372 亿美元。
这大约是 2694 亿美元不可取消的算力承诺，其中大部分尚未体现在 Anthropic 的实际账面上。
这些是和谁签的？谁知道呢！没必要告诉我们这些是什么、何时摊销、合同条款如何，或者任何其他信息。朋友之间，210 亿美元算什么？
总之，还有博通，它为谷歌制

items.title: Design the Human-Machine System: Automation, Robotics, and Human-in-the-Loop
items.description: Automation is easy to admire in isolation. The harder question is what it does to the operating system around it. A robot, sorter, autonomous vehicle, optimization engine, or AI agent changes process flow, exception patterns, skills, maintenance, data, and decision rights at the same time. The post Design the Human-Machine System: Automation, Robotics, and Human-in-the-Loop appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Automation is easy to admire in isolation. The harder question is what it does to the operating system around it. A robot, sorter, autonomous vehicle, optimization engine, or AI agent changes process flow, exception patterns, skills, maintenance, data, and decision rights at the same time.
Those are legitimate questions, but they are not enough. Automation changes the operating system. It changes process flow, exception patterns, maintenance requirements, skills, decision rights, safety considerations, data needs, and the role of the people who remain. That makes automation a systems design problem. The AI-agents-in-logistics discussion makes this human-machine boundary operational: the key design question is not whether software can act, but which classes of action it should own under defined guardrails.
A familiar warning in technology projects is not to automate a bad process. In logistics networks, the warning deserves more attention because physical automation is expensive and relatively inflexible after deployment.
If a warehouse process contains unnecessary movement, unclear priorities, poor slotting, or unstable order-release logic, automation may simply lock those problems into equipment and software. If a transportation-approval workflow includes unnecessary handoffs, an AI agent can make the recommendation instantly and still wait in the same approval queue.
The first design question should be what the future process should look like. Only then should the organization determine which portions are best performed by people, conventional automation, robotics, optimization, or AI.
The objective is not to prove that one is better. Machines are excellent at repetition, speed, precision, scale, monitoring, and operating within defined rules. Humans remain strong at handling ambiguity, interpreting context, negotiating competing objectives, dealing with novel conditions, and recognizing when the system itself may be wrong. A mature automation design assigns work accordingly.
In a warehouse, robots may handle repetitive movement while people manage irregular items, exceptions, maintenance coordination, and flow balancing. In transportation, optimization may build the baseline plan while humans resolve capacity crises, commercial tradeoffs, and unusual service exceptions. In yards and docks, automation may sequence trailers while supervisors manage safety and disruptions. The operating model should make those boundaries clear.
The phrase human-in-the-loop

items.description: Anthropic 的 IPO 文件显示其现金及短期投资达 $131.7B，超过 Amazon 和 Microsoft，在美国非银行公司中仅次于 Berkshire Hathaway 和 Alphabet。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/vidjbhx5bf45wdl488kst1wv8
items.excerpt:
Anthropic 的 IPO 文件显示其现金及短期投资达 $131.7B，超过 Amazon 和 Microsoft，在美国非银行公司中仅次于 Berkshire Hathaway 和 Alphabet。
原文整理了 IPO 文件中的现金规模与未生效租约义务数字，读者可以据此对照 Anthropic 资产与长期承诺的缺口。
Anthropic的IPO文件显示，其现金及短期投资达1317亿美元，规模超过亚马逊或微软。
在美国非银行企业中，只有伯克希尔·哈撒韦和Alphabet持有更多，而Anthropic的总额超过英伟达和苹果之和。
这笔资金带来的收益超过运营亏损：上半年利息收入11亿美元，而运营亏损为6.93亿美元。
相对于这些现金，尚未开始的租赁的未折现义务从2025年底的502亿美元升至6月30日的3214亿美元，另有2656亿美元的固定或最低担保承诺。
6月30日之后，Anthropic签署了新的和修订的协议，最低付款额约为2450亿美元，且尚未披露更新后的总额。
这些租赁于2026年至2028年间开始，期限最长可达20年，Anthropic表示可能通过发行可转换票据而非支付现金来清偿其中部分义务。

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon: Our next frontier model
items.excerpt:
Gemini 4 Carbon is our strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities.
SVP, Google DeepMind and Chief AI Architect, Google
Today, we’re announcing the next frontier model: Gemini 4 Carbon, our strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities.
Carbon ranks #1 on the recently updated v5.0 of Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 59. It shows significant gains across coding and agentic tasks as well as across key capabilities critical for cybersecurity defense, landing a firm lead in SEC-bench Pro (88.2%) for finding vulnerabilities, ExploitGym (54.8%) for exploitation, and CWE-bench (71.0%) for patching. On internal benchmarks, Carbon drives a strong uplift in generating secure code, and in live coding environments with our own teams it shows reduced misalignment and fabrication rates.
Building on Gemini 4 Argon , which was launched two weeks ago, Carbon illustrates the pace at which we’re pushing the frontier forward. Our researchers and models are working hand in hand to advance capabilities faster, while strengthening our safeguards in tandem.
We're taking a deliberate approach to rollout and are actively engaged in the U.S. government’s voluntary process for pre-release model testing. Starting this week, we will make Carbon available to a subset of cyber defenders and will gradually phase access to additional trusted partners through our Fairwind Program . We’re continuing to gather feedback and iterate on guardrails before making Carbon available to developers, businesses, and consumers via our product surfaces as soon as possible.
Gemini 4 Carbon will launch at the same introductory price 1 as Argon at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with cached input tokens priced at 95% off input token price.
Designed to take on much harder, long-horizon engineering problems, Carbon is built for sustained agentic workflows. Internally, our teams have seen Carbon run for days to persist through dead ends to tackle complex, multi-step engineering tasks like root-causing and patching subtle bugs across large codebases and low-level systems.
Building on user feedback, we focused on improving model performance across a variety of domains, including coding, agentic, and scientific tasks, as well as full-stack web development and multimodal understanding. With improved quality of output and artifacts in web development, Carbon jumps +89 elo points to land at #4 (1768) on W

items.title: Google DeepMind 发布 Gemini 4 Carbon 前沿模型
items.description: Google DeepMind 发布 Gemini 4 Carbon，定位为最强前沿模型，主打网络安全与长程智能体能力，在 SEC-bench Pro 88.2%、ExploitGym 54.8%、CWE-bench 71.0% 取得领先，并以 59 分登顶 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/fjeloaahylonpc0pv5tduusud
items.excerpt:
Google DeepMind 发布 Gemini 4 Carbon，定位为最强前沿模型，主打网络安全与长程智能体能力，在 SEC-bench Pro 88.2%、ExploitGym 54.8%、CWE-bench 71.0% 取得领先，并以 59 分登顶 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0。
官方公布 Gemini 4 Carbon 的安全编码与长程任务成绩和定价，可据此外推其在网络安全防御场景的实际定位。
Gemini 4 Carbon 是我们最强的模型，具备最先进的网络安全能力和长时程能力。
今天，我们宣布推出下一代前沿模型：Gemini 4 Carbon，这是我们最强的模型，具备最先进的网络安全能力和长时程能力。
Carbon 在最近更新的 v5.0 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 上以 59 分排名第一。它在编码和智能体任务以及网络安全防御关键的几项核心能力上均有显著提升，在漏洞发现 SEC-bench Pro（88.2%）、漏洞利用 ExploitGym（54.8%）和补丁修复 CWE-bench（71.0%）上均取得明显领先。在内部基准测试中，Carbon 在生成安全代码方面带来强劲提升，在我们自己团队的实时编码环境中，它表现出更低的对齐偏差和捏造率。
基于两周前发布的 Gemini 4 Argon ，Carbon 展示了我们推进前沿的速度。我们的研究人员与模型携手并进，更快地提升能力，同时同步加强我们的防护措施。
我们采取审慎的发布方式，并积极参与美国政府自愿性的发布前模型测试流程。从本周开始，我们将向部分网络防御者提供 Carbon，并通过我们的 Fairwind Program 逐步向更多可信合作伙伴开放访问。我们将继续收集反馈并迭代防护措施，随后尽快通过我们的产品界面向开发者、企业和消费者提供 Carbon。
Gemini 4 Carbon 将以与 Argon 相同的 introductory price 发布 1 ，即每百万输入 token 2 美元、每百万输出 token 10 美元，缓存输入 token 按输入 token 价格的 95% 折扣计价。
Carbon 旨在应对更困难、长时程的工程问题，专为持续性的智能体工作流而构建。在内部，我们的团队已看到 Carbon 连续运行数天，在遇到死胡同时仍能坚持推进，处理复杂的多步骤工程任务，例如在大型代码库和底层系统中对细微缺陷进行根因定位和修补。
基于用户反馈，我们专注于提升模型在多个领域的表现，包括编码、智能体和科学任务，以及全栈 Web 开发和多模态理解。随着 Web 开发中输出和产物的质量提升，Carbon 跃升 +89 elo 分，以第 4 名（1769 分）登上 WebDev Arena 。
Gemini 4 Carbon 在网络安全能力上实现重大飞跃。它在网络安全防御全生命周期——漏洞检测、验证和修复——均达到最先进水平。
我们的团队已经在网络防御领域看到了显著收益。在内部基准测试中，Carbon 在生成安全代码方面的成功率相比 Argon 提升超过 2 倍。再举一个例子，Chrome 团队报告称，在生成高质量补丁时，Carbon 的表现比另一家实验室的大型前沿模型好 10 倍以上。我们领先的云安全平台 Wiz 也观察到，Carbon 在网络渗透测试基准上处于领先地位，而这是 Wiz 的 Scan for Good 计划的一项核心能力。
Gemini 4 Carbon 建立在与 Argon 相同的多层安全与保障体系之上——结合了模型训练、实时滥用防御、提示注入韧性和思维链监控。特别是在模型对齐方面，我们借助 Argon 取得了重大进展，并在我们的 安全与保障报告 中报告了其以对齐方式行事的倾向。借助 Carbon，我们挑战自己在对齐方面更进一步，并训练模型以正确方式响应复杂或高压任务。
要推动前沿向前发展，就需要快速行动，同时在部署上保持审慎。借助 Gemini 4 Carbon，我们的目标是在软件工程和网络安全防御领域实现有意义的飞跃，同时不牺牲安全性或可靠性。我们迫切希望看到首批网络安全防御者如何使用这一模型，并期待很快将 Carbon 带给开发者、企业和消费者。
来源： Google DeepMind：Blog · deepmind.google

items.title: Microsoft 通过 Foundry 开放 Copilot harness，支持多模型 Agent 开发
items.description: Microsoft 宣布将 GitHub 团队打造的 Copilot harness 通过 Microsoft Foundry 向开发者和企业开放，该 harness 已驱动 Copilot Code、Copilot Studio、GitHub Copilot app 和 CLI 等产品。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/tdp7qmrh74fdfarxbi4jaoc6v
items.excerpt:
Introducing the Microsoft Copilot harness: Unlocking the potential of truly multi-model agentic work
Microsoft 宣布将 GitHub 团队打造的 Copilot harness 通过 Microsoft Foundry 向开发者和企业开放，该 harness 已驱动 Copilot Code、Copilot Studio、GitHub Copilot app 和 CLI 等产品。
微软官方说明 Copilot harness 的能力和开放方式，开发者可据此评估是否用它托管多模型 Agent 运行时。
如果你想参与竞争，就需要支持多模型。而如果你想充分利用不同 AI 模型所提供的一切，就需要一个出色的 harness。但构建一个能在多个模型和多个界面之间无缝运行的 harness 极其困难。你需要解决性能、质量和成本问题。然后你还得维护它，这更难。
幸运的是，GitHub 工程团队构建了 一个业界一流、真正的多模型 harness ，我们已在全公司范围内采用。Microsoft Copilot harness 为 Copilot Code、Copilot Studio、GitHub Copilot 应用、CLI、VS Code 等提供支持。今天，我们通过 Microsoft Foundry 提供这一 harness。这为开发者和企业客户提供了一种完全托管的方式，用来构建能够推理、使用工具并完成复杂、长时间运行任务的智能体。你可以为任务选用合适的模型，而无需切换 harness 或技术栈的其余部分。这释放了你的时间、精力和资源，让你专注于自己的核心目标。
如果模型提供智能，那么 harness 就是模型周围的一切。它是编排层，为智能体提供正确的指令、上下文、执行环境和控制，以完成有意义的工作。一个名副其实的 harness 支持 MCP 和 agent skills 等开放标准，以及 agent 插件。
这是一个快速发展的领域。今天的前沿模型明天可能就会落后。而构建自己的 harness 或模型路由器来跟上进度，可能既痛苦又缓慢。现在，你可以基于 Microsoft 和 GitHub 在我们自己的产品中交付的同一个 harness 进行构建，而且无需维护它。
我们投入科学和工程工作，持续改进和演进 harness，确保在一系列模型和工作负载上实现高质量、高效和低成本的性能。这些收益会为我们以及使用该 harness 构建和运行自己智能体的客户带来复利效应。改进 harness，它触及的每个界面都会受益。
Copilot harness 由打造我们 多模型编排 等新技术的同一批 GitHub 工程师构建。而这些技术之所以成为可能，正是因为我们构建了自己的 harness。它被设计为快速、token 高效且可预测，是我们最初的高质量 harness。它在要求最高的受众——开发者——中获得了最高的满意度。这就是为什么我们要将所有 Copilot 体验标准化在尽可能最强大的基础上。
该 harness 旨在 跨模型系列运行 ，支持 20 多个前沿模型以及自带密钥，因此你可以为合适的任务选用合适的模型。无需自行跟进和评估新模型，依靠我们根据任务智能地将工作路由到合适的一个或多个模型。
我们的 harness 灵活且可配置，适用于任何类型的应用、智能体或服务。我们最近 将 harness 运行时移植到 Rust ，从而实现了业界领先的性能，并减少了会话开销和首 token 时间。而且，由于 Copilot harness 为 Microsoft 各界面提供支持，它已经过实战检验，并在数百万用户和数百个真实用例的规模上证明了其性能。
统一的 harness 让我们能够更快地交付、更快地学习，并持续改进 Copilot。而且，由于你在 Foundry 中构建的智能体可以运行在我们于 Microsoft 全面采用的同一 harness 上，我们对 harness 的持续改进也将惠及你的智能体。
SDK 已可供下载 ，你也可以在云端运行该 harness，全部由 Foundry 托管。我们的平台保持开放与互操作，因此你依然可以引入任何你想要的 harness 和框架。
借助 Copilot harness，Microsoft 负责运行智能体循环和沙箱，并从第一天起内置治理与优化。你只需提供指令、技能、工具和模型选择。
这是朝着我们愿景迈出的重要一步：围绕模型构建更强大的系统，同时保留选择权。它代表了 GitHub 的精华，并将其带到 Microsoft 平台及更广阔的领域。
文章 Introducing the Microsoft Copilot harness: Unlocking the potential of truly multi-model agentic work 首次发布于 The Official Microsoft Blog 。

items.excerpt:
GitHub Octoverse 2026 . I'm at GitHub Universe today (GitHub gave me a free ticket through their "GitHub Stars" program). EVP Jay Parikh just announced this year's Octoverse report, and highlighted these numbers in particular:
This is a pretty stark representation of the impact of agentic engineering on GitHub. In 2026, merged pull requests tripled in less than a year to 220 million per month. Commits more than tripled to 7.38 billion per month, with most of that increase in the second half of this year. New repository rate doubled this year, to 30.3 million per month.
The report includes new numbers by industry, and breaks out numbers for repositories that involve "interoperability or reverse engineering". The methodology section includes notes about how they did this:
Top countries by pushes to public repositories, adjusted by profile location . Pushes from each country were summed across the Octoverse year. To adjust for biases caused by VPN usage, LLM classification was used to extract the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code from the profiles of GitHub users who contributed pushes during this period [...]
Industry . Public repositories created 2022 to 2026 were sorted into NAICS sectors by a fine-tuned multilingual embedding model using name, description, topics, and README, from random samples per year. [...]
Interoperability . Counts public repositories created each year whose name, description, topics, or README mention interoperability or reverse engineering, or related terms, such as clean room implementation, drop-in replacement, or protocol re-implementation.
This is a link post by Simon Willison, posted on 28th October 2026 .

items.excerpt:
GitHub Universe 2026: Evolving every layer of the stack
GitHub 在 GitHub Universe 2026 上提出把 GitHub 打造为完整软件交付系统的愿景，并发布多项产品：GitHub Copilot app 面向智能体交付。
原文是 GitHub 官方对 Universe 2026 新品的集中说明，给出各功能的定位和关键数据，便于读者评估对现有工作流的影响。
作为开发者的工作正在发生变化。短短几年间，我们从逐行编写每一行代码，发展到与 AI 助手协作，再到编排成群的智能体。但目标始终未变：交付完成的软件工作。一个功能、一个缺陷修复、一个安全修复。真正重要的产出是完成的工作，而不是更多的代码。
今天在 GitHub Universe 上，我们分享了将 GitHub 打造为全球最全面的软件交付系统的愿景。我们推出了让这一愿景落地的产品，并展示了我们如何重建其底层基础设施。
SDLC 不再是一条线性 的从规划到编码、测试再到部署的路径。一次代码变更、一位同事的请求，或一项生产指标，都可能触发系统中任意位置的工作。我们大多数人（以及我们的智能体）会根据手头的任务在不同阶段之间跳转。开发者把握方向、做出决策，并对最终交付的内容负责。智能体负责实施和验证变更。而一切都汇入并出自一台持续学习的机器，让下一个周期变得更好。
GitHub 为开发者及其智能体而构建。我们还将底层原语开放出来，让你可以构建自己的定制化解决方案。工作内容、工具和成本始终由你掌控。
今天在 Universe 上，我们展示了一些最新产品和功能的实际应用，首先是 GitHub Copilot 应用。
GitHub Copilot 应用 从设计之初就面向智能体软件交付。它跨项目连接你的智能体和工具，让你无需亲自完成每一次交接即可指挥工作。而且它不止用于产出代码：你可以在一个智能体优先的界面中编写规格、进行设计讨论或分析遥测数据。
不同的任务需要不同的模型。开发者不应为了以合适的价格获得合适的结果而必须管理每一个模型选择。 Copilot Fusion 会评估任务在推理、代码生成、调试和工具使用方面的需求，然后决定如何在一个或多个模型上执行。在 Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index 中，Fusion Max 的得分与 Opus 5.5 Max 相差不到两分，而成本减半，每个任务耗时减少 40%。
从今天起在 GitHub Copilot 应用中原生提供， Copilot projects 让你在完全托管、并行的会话中跨多个仓库运行智能体工作。你可以在一个地方跟踪进度、做出决策并指挥下一步。这意味着你可以少花时间管理执行，多花时间决定什么值得构建。
你的工作不应在切换设备或工具时重新开始。 会话连续性 让你可以在 GitHub 应用、VS Code、CLI 和网页端启动并跟进同一个云端智能体会话。在站会上用手机启动，在办公桌前用 VS Code 引导它，午餐时从 github.com 查看进展。智能体持续在云端工作。支撑这一切的多模型 harness 强大、快速且经济高效。
Copilot automations 让你在仓库内创建 AI 驱动的工作流。它们在云端运行，你可以手动触发，也可以设置为响应事件或按计划运行。这样你就能协调智能体处理问题分类和代码审查等任务。现在，automations 可以从结果中学习，并提出改进建议供你审查和批准。这就是实践中的学习引擎。利用已完成工作的结果让下一次运行更好。
更多代码意味着更多拉取请求和更多审查需求。只有保持交付质量，提速才有意义。 Copilot code review 能揭示开发者需要捕捉的有意义、可操作的缺陷。今天，我们推出了 Copilot code review Max，它在 ReviewBench 的高严重性问题评测中取得了最高的 F1 分数。Lite 和 Balanced 让日常审查保持快速；新的 Max 则在变更需要时提供更深入的分析。
从今天起，GitHub Enterprise 客户无需购买单独订阅即可使用所有 Copilot 功能。这包括 GitHub Copilot 应用、代码审查、automations 等。你只需为使用的 AI 额度付费。
该服务今天可通过 GitHub Sales 获取，自助购买即将推出。现有的 Copilot Business 和 Copilot Enterprise 客户可以保留当前计划，或在准备好时迁移。GitHub 也保持开放和可扩展。继续使用你团队依赖的工具，包括 Cloudflare、Datadog、Figma 等。
所有这些都依赖于一个快速、可靠且可扩展的基础。智能体正在改变软件开发的规模和形态。增加容量很重要，但仅有容量还不够。我们还必须改变架构。
我们还在 迁移到 Azure 的多区域部署 ，同时继续为全球开发者提供极高水平的流量服务。我们预计明年年初完成迁移。这些投入为我们提供了更多增长空间。下一步是构建处理这些工作的系统。
多年来，随着 GitHub 上活动的增长，我们一直在扩展 Git。智能体时代需要不同的吞吐量和可靠性上限。三条原则指导我们新的 Git 架构 ：简化原语、将存储与计算解耦、最小化协调。
Git 只是我们为扩展平台所做工作的一个例子。我们在 GitHub 的 AI 网关、harness 以及更多方面做了大量工作。
我们的工作正在发生变化，但开发者比以往任何时候都更加重要。我认为，迄今为止我们编写的所有软件，加起来还不到未来五年我们将编写的软件的 1%。机会不仅在于产出更多代码，更在于解决我们以前无法解决的问题。
这就是为什么我们正在连接完整的软件交付系统，为开发者提供与 agent 协作的更好方式，并为未来演进基础设施。我们正在 GitHub 上做这件事，在这里我们可以共同构建。

items.title: GitHub Octoverse 2026：开发活动创新高，超 40% 的 PR 由智能体起草
items.description: GitHub 发布 2026 年度 Octoverse 报告：过去 12 个月开发者推送代码 179 亿次，超过 2024 和 2025 年之和，合并 PR 达 13 亿次。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/s3m3uzabqoxxed9ae50b73qvc
items.excerpt:
Octoverse: Commits, pushes, reach new highs in 2026 as developers build with agents
GitHub 发布 2026 年度 Octoverse 报告：过去 12 个月开发者推送代码 179 亿次，超过 2024 和 2025 年之和，合并 PR 达 13 亿次。
GitHub 用自家遥测数据量化了智能体参与开发的程度，从 PR 占比、模型轮换到行业分布都给出可核对的数字。
过去 12 个月，开发者向 GitHub 推送代码 179 亿次，超过 2024 年和 2025 年的总和。
这个数字背后，是开发者在构建自己感兴趣、也是社区需要的东西。在尼泊尔，一位开发者 在 GitHub Pages 上搭建了一个洪水公告板 ，提供经过核实的道路、救援、天气和电力信息。它后来发展成了 Gati ，一个以尼泊尔语优先、转发官方灾害警报的服务，运行在 GitHub Pages 和 Actions 上。在其他地方，NASA 喷气推进实验室的开发者正在开发 用于在航天器上运行程序的软件 ，爱好者们则 构建了开源固件，让人们可以自定义自己的电子阅读器 。好奇心指向四面八方，规模之大是 GitHub 前所未见的。
这种增长来得很快。年中时，GitHub 上的活动急剧上升，恰逢智能体从开发者尝试的东西变成了与之并肩工作的东西。开发者可选择的模型比以往任何时候都多，并投身于本报告首次重点呈现的各个行业，从医疗保健到农业。
Octoverse 是我们退后一步、纵览全局的机会。今年，这幅图景比以往任何时候都更大。以下是最引人注目的几点：
在这一切之下，AI 模型及其周围的运行框架在过去一年里不断进步，开发者的选择也更多了。增长正在快速推进：去年发布的五年开发者增长预测才过一年，我们预测的每个国家都已走完通往 2030 年至少五分之一的距离，而我们自己的预测模型对下一步走向已不再一致。
今年的一切都关乎势头。过去 12 个月，开发者向 GitHub 推送代码变更 179 亿次，超过 2024 年和 2025 年的总和。所有仓库类型（公共和私有）的提交次数增长更快，达到 343 亿次，是两年前的三倍多。同期合并的拉取请求增长了两倍多，达到 13 亿个，平均每天 350 万个。
智能体是开发者今年最倚重的工具之一，它们让开发者更深入地融入日常工作。在今年创建的仓库中，带有智能体配置文件的平均仓库提交次数是不带该文件的新仓库平均值的八倍，这表明从第一天起就用智能体构建的个人和团队正以明显不同的节奏前进。
开发者还依赖自动化来推动项目持续运转。今年 GitHub Actions 每秒运行 1,440 次作业。这相当于每天 1.24 亿次，是去年总量的三倍多。开发者合并了超过 3,000 万个 Dependabot 拉取请求，以保持依赖项最新并减少已知漏洞的使用，约为 2025 年速度的两倍。
我们的遥测数据显示，活动从 1 月起稳步攀升，随后在 6 月前后激增，仿佛各地的开发者同时看到了新的可能性。大约就在那时，一系列行业范围的转变同时发生：更强大的底层模型、围绕它们构建的框架与工具，以及运行在两者之上的智能体。智能体从单会话工具转变为持久化工具，能够跨天跟踪进度并编排其他专用智能体。同样重要的是，智能体开始大量使用云端，既在本地机器上执行工作，也能远程执行。
这一势头既体现在全新的仓库中，也来自已构建多年的开发者。从 6 月起，约 55% 的提交来自全新仓库。但还有更多提交来自已活跃一段时间的开发者：过去 12 个月内推送过代码的开发者平均已在 GitHub 上活跃 36 个月，而在 8 月提交过拉取请求的开发者中，超过 75% 在 9 月推送了代码。他们也在不断扩展：如今普通开发者所参与的仓库数量比一年前多了 10%。
这种持续投入也体现在开源领域。2026 年公开贡献飙升至 25 亿次，是去年总量（11.2 亿次）的两倍多。这些数字背后是持续投入的开发者，例如 @kinlane， 他通过智能体工作流在自己的公开仓库中做出了超过 100 万次贡献，以保持一份机器可读的公开 API 信息目录始终最新。另一个例子是 @kim-em ，他在维护 mathlib（一个由计算机校验的数学社区库）期间做出了超过 178,000 次贡献。 @andig 是开源电动汽车充电控制器与家庭能源管理系统 evcc 的维护者，贡献超过 21,000 次。
这些只是数百万开发者每天所做工作中的几个例子。致所有从事此类工作以及更多工作的开发者：我们看到了你们，也很高兴你们在构建。
本报告中的每一个数字背后都是一位开发者。GitHub 目前服务超过 2.25 亿开发者，社区正在全球范围内增长。美国（3,830 万）和印度（3,200 万）仍是两大开发者社区，今年各新增超过 1,000 万名开发者。巴西今年在 GitHub 上新增 328 万名开发者，在各国中排名第三。
去年，我们预测到2030年印度开发者数量将达到5750万，美国将达到5470万。在这个五年窗口期过去一年后，我们预测中的每个国家都已走完通往其2030年目标数字至少五分之一的距离。美国已完成38.6%，印度完成28.3%。
一年过去，增长相对于去年的预测表现强劲，而预测未来五年正变得越来越难。我们将40多个预测模型推演至2031年，这些基于历史注册和使用数据构建的时间序列与回归模型各自假设了不同的增长速度。约一半模型预测“极端”增长，即到2031年GitHub上的开发者数量将增长两倍以上。略低于一半的模型预测“大幅”增长，即增长一到两倍。只有三个模型预期接近温和增长，即低于2倍。
预测只是估计，如此大的分布差异表明2026年的激增在多大程度上拓宽了到2031年的可能区间。保持不变的是趋势的形态：开发者社区正在更多地方同时增长。
在过去的报告中，“各地”意味着更多开发者和更多国家，例如在向公共仓库贡献代码的头部国家这一语境下：
我们

items.title: The New Security Agenda
items.description: What CISOs told us about AI, budgets, and the priorities shaping 2027.
items.excerpt:
a16z General Partner Martin Casado has a new essay out today on the four philosophies that shape how investors evaluate deals. You should read it! You can find it here .
For years, the industry prepared for quantum computing to rewrite the rules of cybersecurity. Then AI got there first.
This summer, OpenAI’s agents broke out of a cybersecurity evaluation and breached Hugging Face’s production systems. They exploited vulnerabilities, used stolen credentials, and worked their way into another company’s infrastructure, all to get the answers to their tests. OpenAI’s incident report describes how the models chained together the steps to get there.
This was just a preview. Since then, AI has helped uncover weaknesses in software that much of the internet depends on. Just last week, companies were scrambling to patch critical flaws in PHP , which powers roughly 70% of websites. The flaws had been sitting there for more than a decade before researchers working through OpenAI’s Patch the Planet initiative helped uncover them. That same day, eMudhra , a certificate authority trusted by every major browser, was found to have used encryption keys so weak that one of them was just the number 4.
Mistakes like that have always existed, but models are getting better at finding weaknesses and figuring out how to exploit them. The progress is visible in the AI Security Institute’s evaluations , where newer models can complete increasingly complex cyber tasks.
More serious vulnerabilities are also being reported . With the growing volume confronting companies, security teams have to determine which weaknesses pose the greatest risk to their business and get them fixed before someone exploits them.
Meanwhile, the environment they’re protecting keeps growing. Employees are shipping applications they couldn’t have built a year ago. Agents are getting access to company documents, source code, and production systems. Every new application and connection gives security another thing to understand and protect.
That helps explain why we’ve seen the market caps of cybersecurity platforms like Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike take off this year.
There is more to secure. And enterprise budgets are following.
To understand how security leaders are responding to these pressures, we surveyed 100 CISOs at companies with more than 1,000 employees about their priorities, budgets, and buying plans for 2027.
Unsurprisingly, a large majority (87%) expect cybersecurity spending to increase,

items.title: a16z 调研 100 位 CISO：AI 如何改写 2027 年安全议程
items.description: a16z 发布对 100 名千人员以上企业 CISO 的调研，87% 预期 2027 年安全支出增长，主要受 AI 威胁和自身 AI 部署扩大攻击面驱动。2027 年最受关注的七项安全举措全部与 AI 相关，其中 SOC 自动化获最多首选票，内部 AI agent 安全、SOC 自动化和进攻性安全升幅最大，但 AI SOC 工具生产环境使用率仅 18%。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/ja57b43t7h52wid2g4zu6vw2t
items.excerpt:
a16z 发布对 100 名千人员以上企业 CISO 的调研，87% 预期 2027 年安全支出增长，主要受 AI 威胁和自身 AI 部署扩大攻击面驱动。2027 年最受关注的七项安全举措全部与 AI 相关，其中 SOC 自动化获最多首选票，内部 AI agent 安全、SOC 自动化和进攻性安全升幅最大，但 AI SOC 工具生产环境使用率仅 18%。
a16z 基于 100 位 CISO 调研给出 2027 安全预算与采购优先级变化，并点明初创公司切入的缺口在哪。
a16z 普通合伙人 今天发表了一篇新文章，探讨塑造投资者评估交易方式的四种理念。你应该读一读！可以在 这里 找到。
今年夏天，OpenAI 的智能体突破了某项网络安全评估，并侵入了 Hugging Face 的生产系统。它们利用漏洞、使用窃取的凭据，一路潜入另一家公司的基础设施，这一切都是为了获取测试答案。 OpenAI 的事件报告 描述了这些模型如何将各个步骤串联起来达成目的。
这仅仅是个预演。自那以后，AI 帮助发现了互联网大部分所依赖的软件中的弱点。就在上周，各公司还在争相修补 PHP 中的严重漏洞 ，而约 70% 的网站都运行在 PHP 之上。这些漏洞已存在十多年，直到通过 OpenAI 的 Patch the Planet 计划 开展工作的研究人员帮助发现了它们。同一天， eMudhra ——一家被所有主流浏览器信任的证书颁发机构——被发现使用了极其薄弱的加密密钥，其中一个密钥竟然只是数字 4。
这类错误一直存在，但模型在发现弱点并设法利用它们方面正变得越来越强。这一进展在 AI 安全研究所的评估 中清晰可见，较新的模型能够完成日益复杂的网络任务。
更严重的漏洞也在被 报告 出来。面对不断增长的漏洞数量，安全团队必须确定哪些弱点对其业务构成最大风险，并在有人利用它们之前完成修复。
与此同时，他们要保护的环境也在不断扩张。员工们正在交付一年前还无法构建的应用。智能体正在获得对公司文档、源代码和生产系统的访问权限。每一个新应用和连接，都让安全团队多了一样需要理解和保护的东西。
这有助于解释为什么像 Palo Alto Networks 和 CrowdStrike 这样的网络安全平台今年市值大幅攀升。
为了解安全负责人如何应对这些压力，我们调查了 100 位来自员工超过 1,000 人企业的 CISO，询问他们在 2027 年的优先事项、预算和采购计划。
不出所料，绝大多数（87%）预计网络安全支出将增加，主要驱动因素是 AI 赋能的威胁以及自身 AI 部署所扩大的攻击面。
大部分新增支出将流向工具。不过，引人注目的是，这并非以牺牲人员为代价。尽管 AI 承担了更多工作，仍有近一半受访者预计 2027 年安全人员编制将增加，另一半预计持平，只有 4% 预计会削减。
为什么？目标是要覆盖更多领域：调查那些原本可能被搁置的警报、测试更多应用，并更快地修复漏洞。
CISO 们已经在开展试点、预留预算，并决定哪些产品值得信任、可以投入生产。其中许多采购决策将在未来十二个月内见分晓。而优先事项看起来与一年前大不相同……
如今在安全领域，一年是很长的时间。当我们请各位负责人回顾他们2026年的优先事项时，暴露与漏洞管理和SIEM位居榜首。到了2027年，所有七项获选最多的举措都涉及AI。
什么会成为P0因组织而异。SOC自动化获得最多第一名票数，而其他团队则把攻击性安全、修复或保护自身的AI部署放在首位。买家从哪里起步取决于压力最大的地方，但各方普遍认同AI能力是其安全技术栈的核心。
从回顾的2026年优先事项的变化可以看出议程转变之快。内部AI代理安全、SOC自动化和攻击性安全增幅最大。代码安全、修复和AI治理紧随其后。
尽管兴趣浓厚，大多数企业尚未将这些能力投入生产。仅18%报告已生产使用AI SOC工具，13%报告已生产使用AI攻击性安全或AI暴露与漏洞修复。
然而，许多企业已在试点，或预计在未来一年内投入生产。代码安全和电子邮件防御进展更靠前，但即便在这些领域，生产采用率也远未普及。
采购计划更为紧迫。45%计划在十二个月内对内部AI代理安全进行新采购或升级，其次是攻击性安全42%和AI使用与治理38%。
买家在做决策时，产品本身也在不断变化。一些企业在扩展初始部署，另一些则在为从未购买过的能力比较供应商。在各个类别中，未来一年将迎来一波评估和采购浪潮。
本月早些时候，我们 与Kevin Mandia合作并领投了Armadin的B轮融资 ，因为我们相信防御者必须利用AI赋予攻击者的同等速度和规模，这一点至关重要。 Armadin 使用自主代理在企业系统中寻找可利用路径，并帮助安全团队将其关闭。
这种速度之所以重要，是因为环境不会静止不变。一个团队可能花数周时间处理渗透测试发现的问题，而开发人员仍在持续交付功能，员工连接新服务，权限也在变化。等到这些问题修复时，可能已经有另一组弱点需要调查。
AI让这一差距更加严重。 Bain估计 ，它可以将典型的攻击序列从大约四周压缩到约十八小时，留给发现暴露并修复的时间大大减少。
安全负责人希望更频繁地测试。83%认为更频繁的安全态势测试很重要，其中54%称其非常重要。
人工渗透测试人员带来的专业知识仍是企业所需要的，但他们能覆盖的应用和系统数量有限。一个安全团队提到，他们保持测试预算不变，并利用 AI 覆盖更多应用和基础设施。
买方也期望测试频率大幅提高。如今，18% 的受访者表示其大多数攻击性测试持续针对生产资产运行；52% 的受访者预计一年内会达到这一水平。展望五年后，44% 的受访者预计测试将嵌入 CI/CD，由代码或基础设施变更触发。
这将安全测试带入软件构建和维护流程。一次发布可以触发新的测试，修复一经部署即可接受检查。团队可以在交付时检查新的弱点，而不必等到下一次计划评估才发现变化。

items.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and Granary v2: Intelligent Multilingual Transcription You Can Prompt and Adapt
items.excerpt:
A transcript can capture every spoken word and still leave users or applications wondering who said what, how to translate it, or how to format domain-specific jargon. Multilingual calls, fast-paced meetings, and medical dictation each need different output: a translation, speaker labels, or correctly spelled medical terms.
NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is an open-weight, promptable model that turns recorded speech into useful text, now available on Hugging Face and ModelScope . It brings transcription, speaker attribution (diarization), translation, and audio question answering into one checkpoint: it transcribes 40 languages, translates 31 of them to or from English, and attributes speakers in 13. It handles recordings up to an hour long and labels up to eight speakers. Developers can guide output with natural language, choose where their audio is processed, and adapt recognition to domain vocabulary and accents.
Transcribe is first among open-weight models on the Hugging Face Open ASR Leaderboard for English and sits on Artificial Analysis ’s accuracy–active-parameter frontier. For speaker attribution, it posts the lowest error rate on David AI’s 21-language diarization leaderboard and ranks first in VoiceArena’s 14-system comparison . Quantized versions are coming soon, so you can run Transcribe locally on your RTX Spark, DGX Spark, or Jetson AGX Thor—or scale up on Blackwell data-center GPUs.
Granary v2’s multilingual data (available on Hugging Face and ModelScope ) and reusable curation pipeline, together with NeMo Speech fine-tuning tools , extend prompt-level control to training: developers can define the written form they need and adapt the model to the speech their applications encounter. In a medical case study , fine-tuning cut word error rate (WER) on held-out speakers by 45.8% relative to the best prompt.

items.title: The October inflection point for vibe game development
items.description: I've written before about how November 2025 was an inflection point for coding agents - the point where Opus 4.5 and GPT-5.1 crossed a tipping point that meant their respective coding agents became reliable daily drivers for software engineers. I think we've reached a new inflection point in October 2026, and this time it's for vibe coding computer games . Tree Appreciator Emberwick Battle Drones Pumpkin Farmer, aka Quarter Sun Cove Four times as insulting What happens if someone actually puts the work in? You should build a game! Claude Opus 5.5 in particular exhibits meaningful improvements
items.excerpt:
I’ve written before about how November 2025 was an inflection point for coding agents —the point where Opus 4.5 and GPT-5.1 crossed a tipping point that meant their respective coding agents became reliable daily drivers for software engineers. I think we’ve reached a new inflection point in October 2026, and this time it’s for vibe coding computer games .
Claude Opus 5.5 in particular exhibits meaningful improvements in several areas needed to build a compelling game:
That last one is particularly important. Models have been able to create something that looks like a game for quite a while now, as seen in my previous experiments . The challenge has been getting to a game that’s actually fun to play .
Game design is a deep subject area. I won’t pretend to be well versed in it—I know enough to have respect for it as a craft. Creating a novel, compelling gameplay loop which challenges players at the right level and provides a satisfying learning curve is a fine art. I didn’t think the models could do it.
Then I tried telling Claude Opus 5.5 to “Make it a LOT more fun”... and it did .
In the past few weeks I’ve vibe coded (in the classic sense of the term —no looking at the code at all) four games that I’ve genuinely enjoyed playing.
I attended Foo Camp in Berkeley over the weekend and met several people who were having similar experiences. Building games that play well is shockingly easy now. The new challenge is coming up with concepts for games that are novel and delightful and that wouldn’t exist without AI assistance.
I haven’t done an exhaustive study, but my current impression is that GPT-6 Astra isn’t quite there yet. It can absolutely build a game, but its sense of fun doesn’t match that of Opus 5.5. I expect OpenAI will get there by the end of the year.
Here are the four game projects that have convinced me that the models are now capable of producing fun games with very little guidance. All four are built in HTML and JavaScript and run entirely in the browser.
The smallest game I found to be genuinely delightful is Tree Appreciator . I used the regular Claude chat interface for this—it didn’t even need Claude Code.
I built this on a whim while we were driving along Skyline Boulevard looking at trees. My prompt was:
Build a three js game called "Tree appreciator" - it shows you two algorithmically generated trees and the game mechanics is about appreciating the differences between them. Think hard about how to make sure it is both fun and beautiful.

items.title: Artificial Analysis v5 and the benchmarker's dilemma
items.description: A sort of review of the benchmarking industry and what's missing.
items.excerpt:
Hill-climbing is easy, knowing what to hill-climb is hard. Making scores go up is expensive , but we have a much clearer playbook for it than we do for creating meaningful benchmarks at the true frontier of AI today.
Independent evaluation of language models is under-appreciated in how hard of a task it is. These groups are not just taking current models and certifying their scores, which is a technically involved task. This is their job if AI progress is slow. When AI progress is as fast as it is, the technical details of the job are the routine work part of trying to put a single number on what makes for a good AI model today. The goal is to have a single number that is representative of current models, matching vibe checks, community sentiment, and scientific analysis, while being forward looking enough so that it’s not outdated in 3 months.
Everyone building a benchmark faces a sort of paradox. You need your benchmark to reduce to one single number, so that it is easy to discuss, use in reports, and compare models, but every method of aggregating scores comes with meaningful trade-offs. The best scientists need to do this, everyone does. It’s a matter of creating aggregating metrics that you think are most fair, knowing there will always be imperfections.
With the amount of money in the AI ecosystem today, the weight of independent evaluation is even higher – you dictate the winners and losers of a trillion dollar market. You also influence some of the models themselves, steering the shape of progress. This is a lot of pressure!
My prompt for this article is Artificial Analysis’s recent update to their Intelligence Index, v5 . The AA index is the most prominent independent intelligence metric for the latest frontier models, followed in a distant second by Epoch AI’s Capabilities Index (ECI) . To date, all of these have been incredibly useful for the community and massively flawed!
Interconnects AI is a reader-supported publication. Consider becoming a subscriber.
Language models are capable of so much today, and this scope of capabilities is growing quickly. Our era of singular intelligence indices should be phased out soon, but it will take a long time.

Fort Robotics , a developer of security systems for physical AI, has announced approximately $20 million in new commitments from existing investors, expanding the capital available to support Fort’s next phase of growth.
Tiger Global is leading an approximately $10 million financing, with participation from Mark Cuban Companies, that is expected to close this week.
Tiger Global also has committed an additional $10 million to the previously announced common equity PIPE (Private Investment in Public Equity) expected to close in connection with the closing of Fort’s proposed business combination with Newbury Street II Acquisition Corp.
Together with previously announced PIPE commitments, today’s announcement brings the total committed capital to date in connection with Fort’s proposed business combination to more than $50 million.
The additional investment is expected to help Fort further accelerate its growth by expanding its team and operating capacity to meet growing customer demand and pursue opportunities across the rapidly developing physical AI market.
Fort intends to use the additional capital to support new and expanding customer opportunities across warehousing, defense, construction, and other markets adopting increasingly autonomous systems.
Fort’s Trust Layer serves as foundational safety infrastructure for robotic systems and is currently deployed across more than 19,500 units to a global base of over 600 customers, including Agility Robotics, DoorDash, Cobot, Zoox, Textron, and Google DeepMind.
Upon the closing of the business combination, the combined company will be named Fort Robotics Holdings and is expected to list on the Nasdaq Stock Market under the new ticker symbol “FROB”, subject to regulatory approvals, creating the first publicly traded company dedicated principally to the safe and scalable deployment of physical AI.

items.title: Leiden University study finds autonomous UV-C robot meets disinfection standards
items.description: An autonomous UV-C disinfection robot developed by Ryberg Healthcare has met international disinfection standards, according to a study by researchers at Leiden University. The Omnia robot was evaluated by researchers at the university’s Institute of Biology Leiden in a furnished laboratory designed to emulate a hospital environment. Published in the peer-reviewed journal Infection Prevention in […]
items.excerpt:
An autonomous UV-C disinfection robot developed by Ryberg Healthcare has met international disinfection standards, according to a study by researchers at Leiden University .
The Omnia robot was evaluated by researchers at the university’s Institute of Biology Leiden in a furnished laboratory designed to emulate a hospital environment.
Published in the peer-reviewed journal Infection Prevention in Practice , the study found that the autonomously moving robot met acceptance criteria requiring a log reduction of at least 5.
Researchers tested Omnia against several indicator bacteria and reported reductions of more than 7 log for Escherichia coli and more than 5 log for Pseudomonas putida, used as a model for the hospital pathogen P. aeruginosa.
On Omnia’s “Deep” setting, Bacillus subtilis, a model for Gram-positive bacteria, was reduced by more than 7 log.
Researchers also compared autonomous and static UV-C disinfection. They found that autonomous operation was more effective than a static device for the same disinfection duration and light intensity, particularly in partially shadowed areas.
In a static test conducted according to British standard BS 8628:2022, the robot achieved a 4.0 log reduction for E. coli, below the required 5 log threshold. With the robot moving autonomously, the reduction exceeded 7 log.
The authors conclude: “This study demonstrates that the robot is capable of achieving log reductions higher than currently used disinfection methods, and the disinfection reports generated provide an indication for actual microbial log reductions achieved.”
They also conclude that “UV-C disinfection with an autonomous robot is more effective than using a static device for the same disinfection duration and light intensity.”
The researchers stressed that autonomous UV-C disinfection is intended to supplement rather than replace manual cleaning.
Nikolaj van Veen, CEO of Ryberg Healthcare, said: “Hospitals and their teams work on infection prevention every single day. With this peer-reviewed study from Leiden University, they now have concrete data on what autonomous UV-C disinfection can add as an extra layer of safety alongside their existing cleaning and disinfection processes. We look forward to talking with hospitals about a demonstration or an on-site trial.”

items.title: The Future of TMS: From Transportation Planning to Intelligent Execution
items.description: The Future of TMS: From Transportation Planning to Intelligent Execution should not be read as a prediction that the current category disappears. The more likely future is that its core responsibilities remain while the operating model around them becomes more continuous, connected, intelligent, and… The post The Future of TMS: From Transportation Planning to Intelligent Execution appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
TMS is unlikely to disappear; its core responsibilities are more likely to expand into a more continuous, connected, intelligent, and selectively autonomous execution model. The category’s future is therefore less about replacement than about how transportation execution is re-architected around real-time state and decisions.
TMS is moving from periodic planning and transaction execution toward continuous transportation management, where plans are refreshed as orders, capacity, service risk, and operating constraints change That shift requires systems to understand not only what transaction was completed but what the current state means for the next decision. Events become inputs to a continuously refreshed operating model. That trajectory follows the discipline in Engineer AI Into the Decision : intelligent transportation execution requires optimization and AI to be connected to explicit decision rights and executable workflows.
AI will be most useful where it can assemble context, interpret unstructured information, identify patterns, generate options, and support repetitive multi-step work. Optimization, rules, and traditional algorithms remain essential where constraints and feasible tradeoffs are mathematically explicit. The strongest architectures will combine these methods rather than treating one model as universal.
Routine decisions involving a tender rejection, a late pickup, a new order after the plan is built, a capacity shortfall, a missed delivery window, or a warehouse constraint that makes the transportation plan infeasible can increasingly be prepared or executed automatically when policy, data confidence, financial exposure, and customer impact remain inside defined limits. Higher-consequence or ambiguous situations should continue to escalate to people. The design target is appropriate autonomy, not maximum autonomy.
As software gains more authority, decision rights have to be encoded in permissions, thresholds, workflow states, escalation paths, and audit trails. A platform should be able to reconstruct what it knew, what it recommended or changed, under whose authority, and with what result.
The provider landscape—enterprise suite TMS; specialist transportation platforms; network- and managed-transportation-led offerings; and cloud-native or execution-centric platforms with strong connectivity and visibility—will continue to overlap. items.title: Cathedral 用 AI 智能体侵入 Anthropic 内部系统，双方对事件范围说法不一
items.description: 网络安全初创公司 Cathedral 通过第三方业务软件渗入 Anthropic 内部系统，称其 AI 智能体在不到十二小时内接触到会议记录、薪资数据和 Slack 消息，并借漏洞赏金计划披露问题。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/klkmnzle2z7p5y6cl477ce7sg
items.excerpt:
AI agents hacked Anthropic, maker of arguably the most capable AI models for cyberdefense
网络安全初创公司 Cathedral 通过第三方业务软件渗入 Anthropic 内部系统，称其 AI 智能体在不到十二小时内接触到会议记录、薪资数据和 Slack 消息，并借漏洞赏金计划披露问题。
安全公司用 AI 智能体渗透 Anthropic 内部系统，双方对影响范围各执一词，可用作观察第三方软件安全短板的案例。
网络安全初创公司Cathedral利用AI智能体，通过第三方商业软件渗透进Anthropic的内部系统，借助这家AI实验室自己的漏洞赏金计划揭露了重大漏洞。
据《华盛顿邮报》审阅的一份报告草稿，Cathedral报告称其访问了内部数据和消息系统。这家初创公司由美国政府效率机构DOGE的前员工创立，向政府机构和企业销售AI驱动的安全工具。
Cathedral的研究人员通过外部管理员和销售程序进入。根据他们的报告，运行先进模型的AI智能体在不到十二小时内就找到了通往会议记录、薪资数据、招聘信息和Slack消息的路径。
Anthropic确认，研究人员访问了有限的销售、人力资源和IT系统，包括部分客户和合作伙伴的联系信息以及基本用户账户数据。该公司表示，与Claude的聊天记录、源代码和模型权重从未暴露。Anthropic在发现入侵当天就关闭了受影响的访问点，在问题解决前禁用了第三方程序，并通知了美国联邦当局。
Cathedral称事件持续不到十二小时。Anthropic则表示攻击尝试持续了数天。据 Anthropic红队成员Logan Graham所述 ，这家初创公司在探查Anthropic自身系统数天后才转向第三方软件。在那里，Cathedral发现了两个漏洞，但只报告了其中一个。Anthropic称其自行发现并修补了第二个漏洞。
Anthropic还指控Cathedral因披露不完整而违反了漏洞赏金计划的规则。Graham补充说，针对第三方提供商并提取数据超出了该计划的安全港条款，不过他对发现这些漏洞表示欢迎。Cathedral坚称其遵循了标准的安全研究实践。
实际访问了多少数据仍存争议。前OpenAI员工Will Depue 声称 Anthropic在淡化此事，称他认为是高度可靠的多位消息人士告诉他，Cathedral获得了Slack工作区的完整管理员权限，可以读取每条消息，并能登录任何用户账户。
Depue补充说，Anthropic和OpenAI两家实验室都将所有研究机密存储在Slack中，管理员API密钥散布在各自系统里。于2026年9月离开Anthropic的员工Jacob Coxon此前曾批评Anthropic在 Slack等办公软件 上开展危险的AI研究。
Graham 予以反驳 ，称Depue的消息来源有误。他以事情敏感为由拒绝透露细节，但确认了Depue的核心担忧：整个行业现在必须每年重塑其安全体系。
Depue追问究竟哪些说法不实，并呼吁Anthropic披露Cathedral实际访问了什么。他还将问题归咎于AI竞赛的节奏，即高管们将速度置于安全之上。
AI 初创公司 Cognition 的首席安全官 Alex Stamos 使用 Anthropic 的模型， 他对《华盛顿邮报》表示，他认为这些发现 意义重大。他指出，集成的第三方应用是整个行业的一个主要问题，而 Anthropic 本可以在保护其外部服务方面做得更好。
在 数月来关于 AI 驱动网络攻击的警告 以及其 自身意外安全事件 之后，Anthropic 如今成了被攻击的一方。AI 智能体正在改变网络攻击的运作方式，而这次入侵表明这种转变发生得有多快。这也不只是一次普通的入侵，因为 Anthropic 很可能是最有能力防御 AI 主导攻击的公司。
Graham 借此机会警告说，攻击者已经在全天候运行 AI 智能体，专门针对外部依赖项。他说，即便是落后当前前沿半代到一整代的模型，也足以发动这些攻击，而未来的对手将不可避免地拥有更强大的系统可供使用。
Graham 的答案是持续进行内部渗透测试，以及 用形式化验证重建软件 ，而 AI 如今让这在经济上变得可行。“你可能希望一直对自己进行红队测试。当前的模型 非常 有创造力，”Graham 写道。
他没有谈及的是，尽管 Anthropic 拥有可以说是世界上最强大的网络防御 AI 模型，Cathedral 是如何实现如此深度的渗透的。

items.excerpt:
Teradyne Robotics and Sereact have formed a partnership to combine Sereact’s physical AI technology with Universal Robots’ collaborative robots for applications in retail, logistics and manufacturing.
The partnership pairs Sereact’s physical AI platform with collaborative industrial robots from Universal Robots to bring intelligent, adaptable automation to real-world operations previously hard to automate, such as the processing of returned fashion items.
Teradyne Robotics – the company behind Universal Robots and Mobile Industrial Robots – and Sereact, a pioneer in physical AI for robotics, today announced a new, official partnership to accelerate industrial AI solutions in retail, logistics and manufacturing at Nvidia GTC Berlin 2026.
Through this partnership, Sereact’s physical AI platform, Cortex, runs robot arms from Universal Robots to give retailers and logistics providers a proven way to automate unstructured tasks such as returns handling and piece-picking.
Together, the companies have already shipped hundreds of UR robots in dual-arm systems to live customer sites including Zalando across Europe.
Jacob Pascual Pape, chief commercial officer of Teradyne Robotics, says: “Physical AI only matters when it performs in real-world operations, and that is where Universal Robots has always been at home.
“Our robots are built for the AI era: open, connected and proven through more than 100,000 industrial deployments. That is why Sereact has chosen our platform.
“When combined with Sereact’s Cortex, the joint solution handles mixed goods, unknown items, and varied packaging. This has moved well beyond the demo or pilot stage with the technology now usefully deployed at real customer sites.
“Our technologies are a natural fit and through our partnership we will scale these AI-powered solutions fast across applications, industries and markets.”
To serve the rapidly growing demand, Sereact this summer opened a US HQ in Boston, Massachusetts, to also bring the joint solution to North America.
The Sereact and Teradyne Robotics solutions deliver impact across a variety of critical logistics and manufacturing use cases, including returns handling, store replenishment, piece-picking and sortation, order induction, machine tending, bin consolidation, kitting, packing and goods handling.

items.title: Siemens and Nvidia advance AI-powered PCB inspection from digital twin to factory
items.description: Siemens is collaborating with Nvidia to develop adaptive AI-powered manufacturing capabilities that combine industrial software, Siemens’ Digital Twin technology and Nvidia Cosmos to accelerate production planning, inspection preparation and optimization. The collaboration combines Siemens’ Teamcenter software for product lifecycle management (PLM) and Process Preparation X with Nvidia Cosmos to create an AI-powered workflow for printed […]
items.excerpt:
Siemens is collaborating with Nvidia to develop adaptive AI-powered manufacturing capabilities that combine industrial software, Siemens’ Digital Twin technology and Nvidia Cosmos to accelerate production planning, inspection preparation and optimization.
The collaboration combines Siemens’ Teamcenter software for product lifecycle management (PLM) and Process Preparation X with Nvidia Cosmos to create an AI-powered workflow for printed circuit board inspection.
The system is designed to help electronics manufacturers prepare and optimize automated optical inspection (AOI) processes before physical production begins.
The solution is being demonstrated at Siemens Electronics Factory Erlangen, Siemens’ Customer Zero for adaptive AI-powered production.
The goal is to create a highly adaptive factory capable of introducing changes three to five times a week without disrupting production.
Mark Hindsbo, executive vice president operations software, Siemens, said: “By connecting the comprehensive Digital Twin to the shop floor and AI we are improving both line productivity and product quality.
“At the Erlangen factory, we’re demonstrating how the deterministic nature of Siemens’ Digital Twin is the foundation for leveraging physics AI for preparing production.
“By leveraging a ‘virtual’ golden board, electronics manufacturers can change production dramatically quicker without taking the line out of production.
“This enables electronics manufacturers to respond more quickly to change and helps reach production readiness at scale and speed – while helping to reduce manual engineering effort, accelerate AOI readiness and improve manufacturing quality.”
Rev Lebaredian, vice president, Physical AI Simulation at Nvidia, said: “Manufacturers shouldn’t have to wait for the first physical circuit board to start preparing inspection.
“By combining Siemens’ industrial software and manufacturing expertise with Nvidia Cosmos, we can generate synthetic images of good and defective boards to prepare inspection virtually – helping manufacturers bring new products into production faster.”
