We believe we have reached an inflection point where AI systems can function as genuine collaborators in professional work. They quickly complete substantive tasks that might otherwise occupy a skilled professional for several hours, a full day, or longer. AI systems are also becoming increasingly capable of performing tasks that were previously too difficult or costly to complete or surfacing original insights and analyses.
We refer to these AI systems that work alongside humans to perform complex, multi-step work at professional levels as Virtual Collaborators. Virtual Collaborators carry the access rights, system connections, and context that their organizations grant them , which allows them to function more accurately and reliably. They can navigate and use internal tools and execute workflows that span multiple steps that require sustained reasoning. Virtual Collaborators are AI designed to be embedded where work gets done, and our aim is to continue extending them to knowledge workers globally, a population that is estimated to exceed one billion in 2028.

items.title: Latent Space 解读 Anthropic 提交 S-1：拟以代码 AN 上市纳斯达克，H1 2026 营收 16.3B 美元
items.description: Latent Space 汇总解读 Anthropic 公开提交的 S-1 文件，公司计划以代码 AN 上市纳斯达克，营收从 2023 年的 41M 美元增至 H1 2026 的 16.3B 美元，Q2 营收 11.6B 美元同比增长 1,368%，营业利润 974M 美元，H1 2026 毛利率达 85%。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/nbvleghbxraalsahhggnc6qov
items.excerpt:
[AINews] Anthropic files for $2T IPO in 2 weeks: 1400% growth rate, 48% of revenue through cloud partners, 85% margin, $1B op profit in Q2, $134B cash in bank and $10B lifetime burn
Latent Space 汇总解读 Anthropic 公开提交的 S-1 文件，公司计划以代码 AN 上市纳斯达克，营收从 2023 年的 41M 美元增至 H1 2026 的 16.3B 美元，Q2 营收 11.6B 美元同比增长 1,368%，营业利润 974M 美元，H1 2026 毛利率达 85%。
原文梳理了 S-1 中的营收、毛利、现金与算力承诺等关键数字，并汇总多方的看多与质疑视角，方便读者快速理解这份文件的分歧点。
今天是那种对普通工程师受众来说更难报道的日子——他们平时不习惯读 S-1，更不用说 350 页的 史上最不寻常的 S-1 之一 ：
显著的经营杠杆带来了 Anthropic 历史上首个盈利季度（按每季度 10 亿美元 SBC 调整后）：
未来的卖点是到 2028 年为超过十亿知识工作者提供“虚拟协作者”（别说 agent！）：
我们相信，我们已经到达了一个拐点：AI 系统可以在专业工作中充当真正的协作者。 它们能迅速完成实质性的任务，而这些任务原本可能会占用一名熟练专业人员数小时、一整天甚至更长时间。AI 系统也正越来越有能力执行此前过于困难或成本过高而无法完成的任务，或揭示原创性的洞见与分析。
我们将这些与人类并肩工作、以专业水平执行复杂多步骤工作的 AI 系统称为虚拟协作者。 虚拟协作者拥有其组织授予的访问权限、系统连接和上下文 ，这使它们能够更准确、更可靠地运作。 它们可以浏览并使用内部工具，执行需要持续推理的多步骤工作流。 虚拟协作者是旨在嵌入工作发生之处的 AI，我们的目标是继续将它们扩展到全球知识工作者，这一人群预计在 2028 年将超过十亿。
Anthropic 于周一美东时间上午约 9 点公开提交了 S-1。它计划在纳斯达克上市，股票代码为“ANT”，文件显示这家公司已跨入经营盈利，同时背负着巨额算力承诺。
前期铺垫。 时间点由 The Information（ @kimmonismus ）、Fox Business（ @negligible_cap ）和 Bloomberg（ @kimmonismus ）报道。IPO 本身此前预计在 11 月 9 日左右（ @kimmonismus ）。
官方文件。 Anthropic 以标准的注册免责声明宣布了此次提交（ @AnthropicAI ）。EDGAR 链接由 @rishdotblog 发布，股票代码由 @kimmonismus 指出。
营收。 营收从 2023 年的 4100 万美元增至 2026 年上半年的 163 亿美元，同比增长约 14 倍。仅第二季度就达 116 亿美元，同比增长 1,368%（ @futurenomics 、 @kimmonismus ）。
盈利能力。 第二季度营业利润为 9.74 亿美元。上半年经营现金流为 +39 亿美元。头条数字 807 亿美元的上半年净亏损包含与金融工具相关的 811 亿美元非现金费用（ @kimmonismus ）。
资本效率。 Anthropic 累计融资 1411 亿美元。它持有 1124 亿美元现金外加 193 亿美元短期投资。隐含的累计烧钱约为 97 亿美元（ @SemiAnalysis_ ），SemiAnalysis 称这“可能是资本主义历史上最高效的企业规模化”。
算力承诺。 不可取消的承诺延伸至下个十年深处（ @scaling01 ）。其中包括通过 SpaceXAI 为 NVIDIA 驱动的算力提供最高 1205 亿美元，相关协议延续至 2029 年（ @kimmonismus ）。
预训练延迟。 Anthropic 披露其近期推迟了一款新前沿模型的预训练（ @scaling01 ）。
锚定投资者。 Altimeter 表示，除现有持股外，还将“大举”参与此次 IPO（ @altcap ）。
他还引用了被广泛报道但并未出现在 S-1 中的 168 亿美元第三季度数字（ @jaminball ）。
SemiAnalysis 给出的消耗为 97 亿美元；Austen Allred 给出的为 94 亿美元。
现金被引述为约 1320 亿美元（futurenomics）或“当前”1340 亿美元（Ball）。
Austen 声称 2023 年至 2026 年 6 月累计自由现金流为正 67 亿美元，当前自由现金流为每月 5.75 亿美元（ @Austen ）。这与 94 亿美元的累计消耗放在一起显得矛盾，因此对推算出的现金流数字应谨慎对待。
亚马逊和谷歌于 2023–2025 年发行的 113 亿美元可转换债券。约 50 亿美元已完成转换。剩余 62 亿美元本金对应 1086 亿美元的公允价值负债，因为其转换价为每股 2–5 美元，而 H 轮价格约为 59 美元。
这些可转换债券实际上相当于约 18 亿股，而非债务，这一按市值计价的调整构成了 GAAP 亏损的大部分。
其余部分：约 6 亿美元的 SAFE/普通股，以及约 7 亿美元来自 2023 年之前的融资轮次。
2026 年上半年营收的 48%（约 78 亿美元）通过 Bedrock、Vertex 和 Azure Marketplace 流转，高于 2023 年的 11%。
市场费用计入销售、营销与合作伙伴支出，而非收入成本。因此它们从不影响 85% 的整体毛利率。
算力效率。 Aymeric Roucher 推算出每 1 美元算力带来 2.08 美元营收，这意味着算力回本时间不足一年（ @AymericRoucher ）。

items.title: OpenAI 扩大与 Oracle 合作，将 Oracle 应用与数据接入 ChatGPT
items.description: OpenAI 宣布扩大与 Oracle 的合作，将 Oracle 应用和数据接入 ChatGPT，并用 OpenAI 模型驱动 Oracle 新产品。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/zbp5qzehshqnvgimabeu27cb1
items.excerpt:
OpenAI expands partnership with Oracle to bring its apps to ChatGPT
OpenAI 宣布扩大与 Oracle 的合作，将 Oracle 应用和数据接入 ChatGPT，并用 OpenAI 模型驱动 Oracle 新产品。
原文来自 OpenAI 官方宣布，列出了合作的具体产品和 Oracle 的使用数据，可了解企业级 Agent 集成的落地形态。
扩展企业借助 Oracle 在 ChatGPT 中以及通过由 OpenAI 提供支持的新产品所能实现的能力。
OpenAI 与 Oracle 正在将 Oracle 的应用和数据引入 ChatGPT，并用 OpenAI 的模型和产品为新的 Oracle 产品和服务提供支持。双方共同的目标是帮助企业利用 AI 运行核心业务、构建更好的应用并加强安全性。
这建立在双方在 OpenAI API、ChatGPT Work 和 Codex 上的商业合作关系之上。Oracle 报告称⁠ ，ChatGPT 活跃用户达 130,000 名，Codex 活跃用户超过 95,000 名。其招聘团队使用 ChatGPT Work 进行市场调研，过去整理这类调研需要两到四天，现在准备工作只需 15–20 分钟。
OpenAI 与 Oracle 对面向智能体的企业有着共同的愿景：人与 AI 智能体在一个互联的环境中跨业务应用协同工作。我们的目标是让 Oracle 软件更易于发现、使用和管理，提供更简单的管理方式、统一登录，以及由各组织的权限和审批机制管控的访问。这将帮助企业将 AI 扩展到核心业务，并从他们已在使用的软件中获得更多价值。
Oracle 正在开发 Oracle AI Workspace⁠ ，通过与 Oracle 应用和数据的集成，将这一愿景带入 ChatGPT。目标是让人们描述自己需要完成的任务、找到正确的信息，并在一处完成已获批准的业务工作流。
例如，一位新加入财务团队的成员可以使用 ChatGPT 调查成本、了解采购决策，并确定月末结账前还有哪些工作待完成。预期的体验将把来自财务、采购和规划应用的信息汇集在一起，帮助更多员工在所属组织的权限和审批范围内使用 Oracle 软件。
除 Oracle AI Workspace 之外，Oracle 还宣布了使用 OpenAI 模型和工具构建的更新及新产品：
Oracle AI Security Mesh 旨在帮助客户使用 OpenAI 网络安全模型发现并修复应用和基础设施中的漏洞。Oracle 负责管理测试基础设施，帮助客户在授权范围内安全地运用这些能力。

美国的 Oracle 客户可以通过 Oracle Marketplace⁠ 购买 OpenAI API、Codex 和 ChatGPT Work 的访问权限，使用现有的采购流程和符合条件的 Oracle Universal Credits。

items.title: Podcast: The 10 Biggest Forklift Manufacturers of 2026
items.description: Explore the top 10 forklift manufacturers in a countdown-style podcast, from number 10 to number 1.
items.excerpt:
In a supply chain environment heavily impacted by the emergence of autonomous mobile robots, predictive analytics, handheld devices and AI-everywhere, the main driver of products within and without the four walls of a distribution center remains the forklift.
According to the Industrial Truck Association , 216,000 forklifts were sold in the US last year, a 9% increase from the 198,000 sold in 2024. That’s still a long way from the peak of over 340,000 in the COVID years of 2021-22, but it’s nonetheless reassuring to see the market bouncing back.
For many years, MH&L has been tracking the Top 10 forklift manufacturers, and the annual ranking of those suppliers is one of our most popular articles every year. This podcast offers a new way to follow the forklift industry, and borrows a page from the old David Letterman show by counting backwards from 10 down to 1. Click on the player below to hear the countdown.
During his career Dave Blanchard has led the editorial management of many of Endeavor Business Media's best-known brands, including IndustryWeek , EHS Today, Material Handling & Logistics , Logistics Today, Supply Chain Technology News , and Business Finance . He also serves as senior content director of the annual Safety Leadership Conference . With over 30 years of B2B media experience, Dave literally wrote the book on supply chain management, Supply Chain Management Best Practices (John Wiley & Sons, 2021), which has been translated into several languages and is currently in its third edition. He is a frequent speaker and moderator at major trade shows and conferences, and has won numerous awards for writing and editing. He is a voting member of the jury of the Logistics Hall of Fame, and is a graduate of Northern Illinois University.

items.description: 作者总结 Anthropic IPO 招股书的 11 个细节，计划募资约 1000 亿美元、估值或达 1.5万亿～2万亿。收入五个季度涨 30 倍，今年二季度经营利润首次转正 9.74 亿美元，但上半年净亏 807 亿美元，主要来自可转换票据公允价值变动；调整后净利润为正 26.71 亿美元。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/t6evqsenxfytsi8wl7h1urjxr

作者总结 Anthropic IPO 招股书的 11 个细节，计划募资约 1000 亿美元、估值或达 1.5万亿～2万亿。收入五个季度涨 30 倍，今年二季度经营利润首次转正 9.74 亿美元，但上半年净亏 807 亿美元，主要来自可转换票据公允价值变动；调整后净利润为正 26.71 亿美元。
作者通读招股书后拆解了收入增速、算力合同、股权结构和公益机制等细节，读者可以借此低成本了解这份文件里不直观的关键信息。
https://x.com/i/article/2114877522169212928
【X 长文】Anthropic要IPO了，帮大家总结了一下招股书里11个有趣的细节。
昨天晚上，Anthropic终于公开了他们的IPO申请，把他们的招股书挂上了美国证监会的网站。
很多人也都说，A\为了上市，终于当了回人，给大家掏出了Claude Opus 5.5这种究极好的模型，就为了IPO的时候好一点。
这份文件，正好是在我昨晚飞机起飞前发布的，于是就扒了下来，飞机上大概全部扫了一遍，因为这可能确实是我们第一次有机会如此全面地了解Anthropic这家世界顶级的AI公司。
并且这一次计划募集大概是1000亿美金，估值大概能落到1.5万亿～2万亿之间，如果到时候真的能募到这么多，Anthropic应该是目前人类历史上规模最大的一次IPO了，对比之前老马的SpaceX上市时达成的世界纪录，首次发行募资750亿美元，随后承销商全额行使超额配售权，最终募了857亿美元。
我自己看完以后，感觉还挺有意思的，总结了11个我觉得还挺好玩的点，给大家分享一下。
Our employees are known internally as “Ants”
Anthropic的员工，在公司内部都管自己叫“Ants”，一群蚂蚁。招股书上的解释是，这个外号代表的是一种互相协作、不太自我的团队文化，原文用的词叫ego-light。
2020年10月26日晚上，蚂蚁集团在港交所公开了IPO招股文件，准备在上海和香港两地同时上市，计划募资345亿美元，准备在11月5日挂牌交易。
六年后的、同样的10月26日，另一个代码叫ANT的公司，以“蚂蚁”之名，继续冲刺人类历史上最大的IPO记录。
而至于挂牌时间，目前还未确认，不过大家主流说法是，都要等到美国11月3号的中期选举之后。
2023年，Anthropic的收入是4100万美元，同一年，它的利息收入是6900万美元。
那一年，它花在销售和市场上的钱，一共200万美元，2023年超级碗一条30秒广告的均价是700万美元，Anthropic一整年的销售和市场费用，连10秒都买不起。
2025年一季度，收入3.76亿美元。二季度7.87亿，三季度13.82亿，四季度20.40亿。到了今年，一季度47.31亿，二季度115.55亿。
今年二季度，它平均每天的收入是1.27亿美元，2023年一整年挣的钱，现在不到8个小时，就挣回来了。
但光看收入，其实看不出这家公司最核心的变化，我觉得这个变化，藏在收入和算力成本的比例里。
2025年一季度，0.40美元。二季度0.57，三季度0.68，四季度0.69。今年一季度1.40，二季度2.08。
前面整整四个季度，它一直在干一件事，花1块钱买算力，卖出去不到7毛。今年一季度，这条线第一次越过了1。到了二季度，变成花1块挣2块。
1. 训练效率提升。Claude已经越来越多地参与到下一代Claude的研发里，内部管这个叫closing the loop。
2. 推理效率提升，同样的模型能力，需要的算力越来越少。从Claude Opus 5.5的强悍气势就能看出来这一点。
3. 芯片。他们自己同时在四种芯片上训练和跑模型，分别是亚马逊的Trainium、谷歌的TPU、英伟达和AMD的GPU，他们自己做了一套调度系统，最大化的压榨性能和性价比。
所以，也就导致了，今年二季度收入同比涨了1368%，但算力和基础设施的开支只涨了300%。
客户结构也在变，今年一季度，前五大客户贡献了大约36%的收入，到了三季度，这个比例降到了大约21%，而且没有任何一家客户的占比超过10%。
并且财富500强里，超过一半已经是它年消费10万美元以上的客户，但这些公司花在Anthropic身上的钱，平均还不到它们总开支的0.1%，就算是用得最多的前10家，也不到1%。
顺便说一句，当年连10秒超级碗广告都买不起的销售和市场费用，今年上半年是31.68亿美元。
今年2月，它还真去超级碗打了广告，片尾那句「Ads are coming to AI. But not to Claude.」，直接内涵OpenAI要在ChatGPT里放广告。
奥特曼专门发了条长推回应，说这些广告挺好笑的，他也笑了，但他想不通Anthropic为什么要搞这么“clearly dishonest”的东西。
我知道很多人好奇，不是说二季度经营利润是正的吗？那一边经营赚钱，一边净亏几百亿，那这钱是亏到哪去了？
答案在利润表下半截的一行科目，叫可转换票据、衍生负债和SAFE的公允价值变动，今年上半年，这一行是负的724亿。
亚马逊投给Anthropic的钱里，有一大块不是直接买股票，而是以可转换票据的形式给的，可转换票据你可以理解成一张借条，上面写着，以后可以按约定的价格换成股票，截至今年6月底，这批借条的本金还有62亿美元。
问题在于，Anthropic的估值，今年2月是3800亿美元，5月就变成了9650亿。
估值涨得越猛，这张能按老价格换股票的借条就越值钱，会计准则要求，借条多值了多少，Anthropic就得在自己账上记多少亏损。
所以光今年第二季度，这一项就记了596亿美元，招股书自己的解释是，这一季的数字最大，主要就是因为H轮融资把估值抬上去了，另外还有84亿，跟今年新签的几份票据购买协议有关。
所以这种亏损，其实一分钱现金都不用掏，招股书也给了一个调整后的口径，把这些公允价值变动、股权激励之类的项目剔掉，今年

items.title: OpenAI 宣布 AI 模型取得三项科学突破，涉及局部光滑猜想、指数时间假设与杨–米尔斯理论
items.description: OpenAI 于 10 月 27 日宣布其 AI 模型在数学、计算机科学和物理学领域取得三项研究突破。数学上给出了所有维度下局部光滑猜想的证明，从而解决挂谷猜想与斯坦因限制猜想；计算机科学上给出推翻指数时间假设（ETH）的证明，暗示相关计算任务可能有更快算法；物理学上提出量子色动力学及标准模型一种统一完备化的严格存在性证明，涉及杨–米尔斯千禧年难题的一部分。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/jxpzj0z4beg1r0cktwzc0tmwe
items.excerpt:
OpenAI 于 10 月 27 日宣布其 AI 模型在数学、计算机科学和物理学领域取得三项研究突破。数学上给出了所有维度下局部光滑猜想的证明，从而解决挂谷猜想与斯坦因限制猜想；计算机科学上给出推翻指数时间假设（ETH）的证明，暗示相关计算任务可能有更快算法；物理学上提出量子色动力学及标准模型一种统一完备化的严格存在性证明，涉及杨–米尔斯千禧年难题的一部分。
原文梳理了三项成果的数学背景和验证方式，并注明仍待学术界独立确认，读者可据此把握证据强度。
IT之家 10 月 27 日消息，OpenAI 宣布，其 AI 模型在数学、计算机科学和物理学领域取得三项重大突破，展现出 AI 独立发现并证明复杂科学理论的能力，而不只是回答问题或辅助研究。
在数学领域，AI 证明了适用于所有维度的局部光滑猜想，并由此解决 局部光滑猜想与挂谷猜想 。
在计算机科学领域，AI 推翻了 长期被广泛接受的指数时间假设 ，意味着未来可能找到速度更快的算法。
在物理学领域，AI 提出 量子色动力学及杨–米尔斯理论的严格数学存在性证明 ，涉及世界七大千禧年数学难题之一。
OpenAI 表示，数学和计算机科学成果已通过 Lean 数学验证工具进行形式化验证，并公开证明材料；物理学成果正由诺贝尔物理学奖得主等专家参与审查。相关成果仍需学术界进一步独立确认。
1991 年，数学家克里斯托弗 · 索格提出局部光滑猜想，试图解释波在聚焦时的行为。按照该猜想，波即使出现极其强烈的聚焦，也只能持续很短的时间。如果随机选取一个具有代表性的时刻，观察到的聚焦程度总会远低于最极端的情况。
数学中经常出现类似现象：某种现象在最坏情况下可以达到非常极端的程度，但经过平均处理后，实际观察到的情况要温和得多。
局部光滑猜想描述的现象具有基础性意义，因此涉及数学分析的众多问题。其中，挂谷猜想和斯坦因限制猜想都可以由局部光滑猜想推导出来。
2019 年，古思、王虹和张睿翔证明了二维空间中的局部光滑猜想。2025 年，王虹与扎尔又证明了三维挂谷猜想。
OpenAI 的模型此次给出了局部光滑猜想在所有维度下的证明，从而也解决了所有维度下的挂谷猜想和斯坦因限制猜想。证明的关键是一种新构建的辅助偏微分方程。
OpenAI 于 2026 年 10 月 18 日获得 AI 生成的证明，并在第二天完成 Lean 形式化证明。随后，OpenAI 联系外部专家，讨论如何围绕该成果建立合作机制。
根据专家建议，OpenAI 决定直接公开 AI 生成的证明，采用与 10 月 6 日发布研究成果时相同的方式。目前，模型撰写的自然语言证明和 Lean 形式化证明均已上传至公开的 GitHub 代码仓库。
ETH 是计算复杂性理论中一个存在已久的猜想，研究布尔公式可满足性问题的计算难度，与著名的 P 和 NP 问题密切相关。
长期以来，学术界 普遍认为 ETH 成立 。数百篇研究论文以该假设为前提，推导出图论、计算生物学、数据库和计算几何等领域的计算难度结论。
近期，OpenAI 的系统却 给出了 ETH 不成立的证明 ，并通过 Lean 完成了形式化验证。
ETH 被推翻后，研究人员需要重新审视许多计算任务 究竟还能获得多大幅度的速度提升 。新成果也有助于指导更高效算法的研究。不过，要找到能够实现这些提升的算法，并将理论成果转化为实际应用，仍需要大量后续研究。
OpenAI 邀请三位算法设计和计算复杂性理论专家牵头，负责验证、研究和解释这项成果，分别是加利福尼亚大学圣迭戈分校的拉塞尔 · 因帕利亚佐和拉马莫汉 · 帕图里，以及麻省理工学院的瑞安 · 威廉姆斯。
因帕利亚佐和帕图里与弗朗西斯 · 赞恩共同提出了 ETH，并在过去 30 年间围绕该假设发表了多篇具有影响力的论文。
威廉姆斯曾证明 ETH 某些强化版本不成立，也曾以 ETH 为基础推导计算难度结论，并在算法与计算复杂性下界之间建立联系。
OpenAI 接受了合作团队提出的两项要求：首先，公开研究成果的所有原始数据，方便其他研究人员独立验证；其次，由 OpenAI 提供资金，举办一场学术会议，讨论新成果对计算机科学领域的整体影响。
合作团队还邀请学术界共同组织对 ETH 证明的公开审查，并就 AI 研究突破引发的问题展开讨论，包括如何验证成果、如何开放研究资料、如何认定学术贡献，以及未来应如何开展科研工作。
OpenAI 于 10 月 16 日生成了推翻 ETH 的自然语言证明，10 月 17 日又完成了 Lean 形式化证明。随后，OpenAI 开始着手建立前述外部合作机制。
模型生成的自然语言证明 和 Lean 证明 现已在 OpenAI 的公开 GitHub 代码仓库发布。
该成果从严格的数学意义上，证明了四维空间中某些 包含规范场和费米子的相互作用量子场论确实存在 ，其中包括量子色动力学（QCD），以及粒子物理学标准模型的一种统一完备化理论。

粒子物理学标准模型描述了亚原子基本粒子之间的相互作用，涵盖自然界四种基本相互作用中的三种，不包括引力。
由于标准模型本身无法直接推广至任意短的距离尺度，OpenAI 的存在性证明针对的是 包含标准模型规范场和费米子的最简单大统一理论 。

Comau is boosting the development of AI-enabled robotics and automation solutions for industrial applications with Nvidia technologies.
By combining Comau’s deep experience in robotics with Nvidia physical AI simulation libraries and accelerated computing, the companies are paving the way for the deployment of increasingly intelligent and autonomous robotic systems.

The next generation of Comau industrial robot controllers will be combined with Nvidia technology to provide the robust computing power required for advanced AI applications.
The new architecture is designed to support demanding, AI-driven workloads, enabling smarter, more adaptive, and highly autonomous robotic solutions tailored to diverse applications and customer needs.
Furthermore, Comau is integrating its industrial, collaborative, and mobile robot portfolio into Nvidia Isaac Sim – an open source framework built on Nvidia Omniverse libraries for robotics simulation, testing, and synthetic data generation.
Comau is also contributing SimReady OpenUSD robot assets to SimReady Central Library on Hugging Face. The library helps developers discover and reuse validated assets, reducing preparation time for building and testing robotic applications.
Nvidia’s simulation and AI libraries are also supporting the development of intelligent, vision-based applications and the optimization of control strategies for intralogistics equipment.
This includes training AI models for Comau’s proprietary MI.RA vision system family, utilizing reinforcement learning for advanced palletizing and depalletizing tasks.
By using Nvidia Isaac Sim’s high-fidelity physics, Discrete Event Simulation (DES) for logistical workflows, and Nvidia Isaac Lab’s advanced learning capabilities, Comau is creating ultra-precise virtual models.
These models are used to train AI-driven control strategies before they ever reach the factory floor. Developing and validating capabilities within these photorealistic, physics-based simulated environments allows Comau and its customers to drastically accelerate deployment in real-world industrial applications.

items.excerpt:
German supermarket group Edeka is expanding the automated logistics solution at its meat-processing facility with two Pick-it-Easy robots from Knapp .
The AI-powered robots improve the efficiency, flexibility and resilience of the retailer’s supply chain, laying the foundation for future growth.
Edeka’s Nordfrische distribution centre in Lüttow-Valluhn, east of Hamburg, features an automated logistics system supplied by Knapp back in 2019. The processing facility supplies around 650 stores with some 2,500 fresh meat, sausage and deli meat products every day.
Now the system has been expanded with the integration of two robots that operate 24/7 to pick individual items fully automatically, relieving employees from physically strenuous tasks.
Thanks to their AI-supported image-processing systems and intelligent picking technology, the Pick-it-Easy Robots recognise and handle a wide variety of fresh meat products reliably.
With a performance of around 450 picks per robot per hour, the solution supports fulfilment that is efficient, scalable and available around the clock.
The robots also perform other steps in the picking process, such as scanning barcodes and recording the weight of each item. In this way, they reduce manual tasks and further improve process quality.
“Despite our large range of products, we are able to pick a wide variety of items efficiently with the Pick-it-Easy Robot,” says Matthias Biermann, managing director of the Edeka Nordfrische facility. “At the same time, we can ensure 24/7 picking if necessary and take the strain off our employees.”
The expansion of the automated intralogistics solution at the Nordfrische site builds upon years of successful partnership between Knapp and Edeka. Up to 40,000 containers a day are processed in the 86,000-square-foot system, which is maintained at a constant temperature of +2°C.
Both items from Edeka’s adjacent processing facility and meat products from other suppliers are integrated in the process. After goods-in, depalletizing and de-stacking, the meats are stored in a shuttle system with around 70,000 locations, where they are available for further processing.
To fulfil orders in a store-friendly manner, there are various picking areas for items with different turnover rates: ergonomic Pick-it-Easy goods-to-person workstations, Pick-to-Light stations and the two new Pick-it-Easy Robots. This combination provides high flexibility for different order structures and volumes.

items.excerpt:
Partners launch two-way pallet shuttle for high-density pallet storage.
Material handling equipment provider Jungheinrich has entered into a strategic partnership with intralogistics specialist Automha, saying the two companies have developed a two-way pallet shuttle for high-density pallet storage.
According to the partners, their "UP-Carrier GTJ" product solution combines Italy-based Automha's shuttle expertise with Germany-based Jungheinrich's strengths in system integration, software, and lifecycle services. The solution is already deployed in more than 200 projects across over 25 countries.
Jungheinrich says that shuttle systems are becoming increasingly important because they address a collection of growing industry challenges. Specifically, many companies face the challenge of increasing material flow performance without fundamentally modifying existing buildings or infrastructure. And at the same time, requirements for space utilization, productivity, and process reliability continue to grow.
According to Jungheinrich and Automha, their new solution has been developed as an entry point into warehouse automation. It can be integrated into existing warehouse environments and increases storage density without requiring major structural changes. Initially, pallet transport continues to be handled by industrial trucks. But as operational requirements evolve and automation levels increase, transport processes can subsequently be automated. This creates a clear migration path from manually supported operations to a fully automated material flow, they say.
The project also demonstrates Jungheinrich's technology-agnostic integration approach, the company said. Depending on customer requirements, Jungheinrich combines its own technologies with selected partner solutions to create end-to-end automation systems. While four-way shuttles, such as those offered by partner Movu Robotics, are primarily deployed in fully automated high-performance pallet warehouses, the new solution developed together with Automha addresses applications in existing warehouse environments and customers seeking a gradual entry into automation.
"Not every company begins its automation journey with a fully automated warehouse," Tobias Harzer, Chief Automation Officer at Jungheinrich, said in a release. items.excerpt:
After initial rollout in Georgia, logistics provider will add additional units at warehouses in North Carolina and Tennessee.
Contract logistics provider GXO will deploy humanoid robots from Agility at distribution centers it operates in North Carolina and Tennessee , expanding on a 2024 partnership that had previously seen GXO use the same model robots at a Georgia facility that handles inventory for the womens clothing brand Spanx.
Since beginning that Georgia test, Agility’s “Digit” model robot has moved more than 100,000 totes at the Flowery Branch facility, demonstrating its ability to perform repetitive material-handling tasks reliably in an active logistics environment, GXO said.
At that site, the two companies have operated a Robots-as-a-Service (RaaS) agreement under which GXO deployed Digit robots and Agility Arc, Agility’s cloud-based platform for managing robot fleets and integrating them into customer operations. At Flowery Branch, Digit has worked alongside existing automation to move totes and place them onto conveyors.
Under the expanded agreement, Digit will support e-commerce fulfillment at GXO’s Statesville and Lebanon sites, taking on highly repetitive material-handling tasks. Deployments are expected to begin in early 2027 using Digit 4 and will migrate to Digit 5 when it becomes commercially available. The Digit 5 model is designed for cooperatively safe work in close proximity to people and to address a broader range of industrial workflows.
“GXO was the first customer to put Digit to work in live operations under a commercial agreement, and expanding to additional sites is the clearest signal that the value is real,” said Peggy Johnson, CEO of Agility Robotics. “Customers are moving beyond asking whether humanoid robots can work to deciding where they can scale them. Years of experience performing real work in GXO’s operations have shaped how we build, deploy and support Digit, and we’re focused on disciplined execution as we grow this partnership.”
To support that broader commercial adoption, Agility has invested in the infrastructure needed to manufacture, deploy and support humanoid robots at scale, including RoboFab, its 70,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Salem, Oregon, designed for annual production capacity of up to 10,000 robots.
GXO has also trialed humanoid robots from the technology providers Apptronik and Reflex in separate pilots.

items.excerpt:
Survey shows popular strategies are to shop for sales, comparison shop online, and use coupons more often.
More than half of holiday shoppers (56%) say the state of the economy will affect their holiday spending plans this year, according to the National Retail Federation (NRF)’s annual consumer survey conducted by Prosper Insights & Analytics.
Among those consumers, 43% plan to shop for sales more often, 31% will comparison shop online more often, and 29% will use coupons more often, among other strategies to make the season more affordable.
Consistent with recent years, nearly all U.S. adults (91%) plan to celebrate winter holidays including Christmas, Hanukkah, or Kwanzaa. Forty-three percent of holiday shoppers plan to begin browsing and buying for the holiday season before November, in line with 42% last year. Among those starting early, 50% do so to spread out their holiday shopping budgets, while 37% say the prices and promotions are too good to pass up.
Yet while many consumers begin their holiday shopping early, many hold off on making the bulk of their purchases until later in the season, with sales and promotions continuing to play an important role throughout the holiday season. Nearly two-thirds (64%) of consumers say they are likely to wait until Thanksgiving weekend to do most of their shopping, in line with 63% last year.
Consumers continue to shop across a variety of destinations during the holidays. Online remains the leading shopping destination, with 53% planning to shop online. Other popular destinations include grocery stores (43%), discount stores (43%) and department stores (42%).Gift cards remain at the top of consumers’ wish lists, with 47% saying they would like to receive them this holiday season, followed by clothing (44%), books and other media (25%) and personal care or beauty items (24%).
These results come from an NRF survey which asked 8,094 adult consumers about their holiday shopping plans. It was conducted Oct. 1 – 7 and has a margin of error of plus or minus 1.1 percentage points.

Decision Intelligence is forming at the intersection of several established categories, so products can be adjacent in the market while solving… The post The 2026 Decision Intelligence Market Map: Four Provider Archetypes Buyers Should Understand appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
The 2026 Decision Intelligence market is best interpreted through provider archetypes rather than a single universal ranking. The category is forming at the intersection of several established markets, so products can sit near one another competitively while solving materially different decision problems. Four broad archetypes help explain those differences.
These platforms create decision depth through scenario modeling, constraints, tradeoff analysis, planning logic, and optimization. They are often strongest when the decision can be represented mathematically and when the buyer needs to compare feasible futures before committing resources. The provider archetypes are easier to interpret against the physical logistics intelligence-layer model , because each archetype begins from a different position in the path from operating signal to coordinated decision and action.
These providers begin with changing external or operational state: shipment events, supplier risk, weather, geopolitical signals, milestones, or network disruptions. Their differentiation depends on whether they can move beyond awareness into consequence assessment, prioritization, recommendation, and coordinated response.
This group focuses on the workflow between insight and action. It may combine contextual data assembly, agentic work, recommendations, approvals, and execution connectivity across multiple systems. The buyer test is whether the orchestration materially improves the decision rather than simply moving tasks between applications.
Broad platforms can distribute intelligence across an installed application suite, trading-partner network, or enterprise data environment. Their advantage may be reach, shared data, and embedded workflow; the diligence question is whether that breadth produces sufficient decision depth for the buyer's priority use cases.
The same enterprise may need more than one archetype. A planning decision, a logistics disruption, and a supplier-risk response can require different intelligence. The Market Map should help buyers understand where each provider creates value, then validate the relevant decision scenarios in detail.
Archetypes create clarity without pretending the market is static. As providers expand, partner, and embed AI, boundaries will move. The durable buyer discipline is to start with the decision and use the market structure to identify the architectures most likely to improve it.
The four archetypes describe different starting strengths. P

items.title: Anthropic S-1 文件中的五个不寻常细节
items.description: The Verge 梳理 Anthropic 向 SEC 提交的 300 多页 S-1 上市文件，列出五个细节。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/fhbcnmkxg23jig75iu44ijywc
items.excerpt:
Five weird details from Anthropic’s IPO filing
The Verge 梳理 Anthropic 向 SEC 提交的 300 多页 S-1 上市文件，列出五个细节。
原文从 Anthropic S-1 文件中提炼出薪酬、算力支出、创始人投票权和风险披露等此前未报道的细节，读者可借此了解其上市后的治理与资金安排。
Anthropic 已 正式提交 其 S-1 招股说明书至 SEC，这份 文件 旨在让投资者深入了解其业务内情，从高管薪酬、IPO 数十亿美元资金的支出计划，到可能阻碍其雄心壮志的风险因素，均涵盖其中。
这份文件超过 300 页，内容繁多，其中一些披露信息此前从未被报道过。以下是我们初读之后发现的几个最引人注目之处：
根据文件，联合创始人兄妹 Dario Amodei 和 Daniela Amodei 是 Anthropic 薪酬最高的两位高管。去年，首席执行官 Dario 的薪酬总额接近 1800 万美元，其中大部分来自股票和期权奖励。与此同时，总裁 Daniela 获得了 1640 万美元。诚然，这 在大科技公司的薪酬标准中处于较低水平 ，但仍是一笔可观的数目。
这还不是全部。Anthropic 还为 Dario 支付了 275 万美元的“个人安全服务”费用，为 Daniela 支付了 129 万美元的“个人保护、住宅安保和交通服务”费用。Dario 还可以使用私人飞机供个人使用，这又让公司花费了 97,055 美元。
公司表示，其成功“高度依赖”高级管理团队的“持续服务”，尤其是 Dario 和 Daniela，他们对于推进公司的研究和使命“至关重要”。
每份 S-1 文件都会列出一长串可能出问题的事项。Anthropic 也不例外。但除了关于竞争、监管和市场变化的常规警告之外，还有一些不那么传统的风险。
例如，Anthropic 警告称，AI 系统可能造成潜在的“灾难性”伤害，其严重程度甚至可能超出整个“保险行业合计”的承保能力。随着 AI 系统变得越来越复杂，还有一个问题：Claude——或任何其他 AI 系统——是否可能拥有或发展出“某种形式的意识”。这种情况将带来一些相当不寻常的商业挑战。此外，它们还“可能以意外、目标错位或自主的方式行事”，从而损害公司利益。
Anthropic 需要算力已不是秘密，但其支出规模之大令人震惊。文件详细列出了为获取驱动其 AI 模型所需的算力而做出的数十亿美元承诺，其中包括一旦所有计划产能交付后，每月向 SpaceX 支付约 31 亿美元 以获取 Nvidia GPU ，到 2029 年总额高达 1205 亿美元。其他承诺包括到 2033 年向 Microsoft 支出 449 亿美元，到 2033 年向 Google 支出至少 1145 亿美元，以及未来十年向 Amazon 支出 1100 亿美元。
Anthropic 还计划扩大自身的“基础设施版图”，包括在海外，因为其在美国面临越来越多的数据中心开发反对声音。
Anthropic 作为一家公益公司，其公司结构本就有些复杂。但还有一个不同寻常的安排，将使其七位联合创始人即便在公司上市后仍能保留相当大的控制权。通过一家名为“Founder LLC”的独立公司实体，这七人将集体控制关键事项上 50.1% 的股东投票权。Anthropic 表示，这七位创始人“具备独特的资质，能够守护我们的使命”，即通过负责任的 AI 开发造福人类。
市面上的 AI 模型并不少，但谈到“直接竞争”，Anthropic 只点名了另外两家开发者：OpenAI 和 Google。向 SpaceX、Meta 以及 AI 世界的其他公司致哀。

items.excerpt:
Price jumped $0.78 a gallon from August to September, which adds up fast for a truck running at 6.5 miles per gallon, Magnus Technologies says.
Diesel prices have been rising so fast that freight carriers need to update their fuel surcharge rates weekly instead of monthly, or else risk squeezing their profit margins , according to transportation management system (TMS) software provider Magnus Technologies.
That conclusion comes as Austin, Texas-based Magnus reported that the U.S. average retail diesel price rose to $6.29 a gallon in September, up $0.78 from the end of August and 68% above September 2025 levels. Those numbers came from the firm’s “September 2026 Diesel Fuel Snapshot” report.
In fact, September 2026 marked the highest monthly average in U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) weekly data dating back to 1994. All four September weeks priced above $5.00, bringing the 2026 total to 25 weeks above that threshold.
The speed of the price increase from August to September matters most for carriers whose surcharge programs reset monthly or are based on prior-period averages. When prices rise this fast, a surcharge priced off last month’s average trails what trucks are actually paying at the pump, and the difference comes out of carrier margin on every load until the surcharge table catches up. At 6.5 miles per gallon, a surcharge that trails the pump by $0.78 a gallon costs a carrier 12 cents a mile, or about $300 per truck on a 2,500-mile week.
“A fuel surcharge is supposed to make fuel neutral, it’s not supposed to be a profit builder for either side or a huge cost burden for the carrier,” said Matt Cartwright, founder and CEO of Magnus Technologies. “September showed how fast that balance breaks when diesel sets a new record hitting above $6.00. If your surcharge resets based off of last month’s price, you’re paying September’s price at the pump while only getting paid on August’s price. The fix is to re-rate against the published index every week, so both sides know what’s reasonable.”

items.title: Epoch AI 用内部工作任务评测前沿模型：Claude Fable 5.1 与 GPT-6 Astra 平均只得 65%
items.description: Epoch AI 发布 Epoch Automation Reports，把机构内部的图表设计、研究规划等真实任务按人类员工评估标准测试 AI，领先的 Claude Fable 5.1 和 GPT-6 Astra 平均得分 65%，未达到 100% 的可自动化门槛。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/dgly2r4fwb6y80t3im8yqqvt1
items.excerpt:
Epoch AI 发布 Epoch Automation Reports，把机构内部的图表设计、研究规划等真实任务按人类员工评估标准测试 AI，领先的 Claude Fable 5.1 和 GPT-6 Astra 平均得分 65%，未达到 100% 的可自动化门槛。
Epoch 用自家真实工作任务按员工标准评估 AI，解释了 65% 的基准分数为何还不足以转化为自动化和经济影响。
AI 年复一年地不断刷新各项新基准。然而，即便 AI 超越人类的基准清单持续增长，AI 实际的 经济影响 似乎增长得更慢。
这种“生产力悖论”反映了基准测试的几个事实：它们通常被校准为衡量前沿 AI 相较过去能力的进步（而非与人类表现对比）；它们往往局限于性能易于评分的任务；而且 AI 有时会针对基准进行训练，就像高中生被教导应对 SAT 一样。所有这些都造成了 AI 在基准上的得分与其在现实世界中实际能力之间的差距。
去年二月，Epoch 高级研究员 Anson Ho 尝试 将自己的工作自动化，测试 AI 能在哪些任务上胜任——又在哪些地方力有不逮。答案是：它在所有任务上都失败了，但他预测到本十年末情况将不再如此。
最近，我们将这一初步尝试扩展为 Epoch 自动化报告，汇集了我们在 Epoch 定期执行的一系列任务，例如平面设计和研究项目规划，并按照我们对人类工作的同等标准来评估 AI。
在这些任务上评估 AI 比大多数标准基准更费功夫，但更能代表真实工作的挑战：它们要求模型收集上下文、使用工具，并处理 Epoch 人类员工所面对的复杂性。
领先的 Claude Fable 5.1 和 GPT-6 Astra 平均得分 65%。这意味着它们的产出满足了人类员工将被评估的评分标准中 65% 的条目——100% 的得分意味着该任务可以放心自动化。
这些结果并不一定意味着我们在时间或任务难度上已走完自动化的 65%，尽管领先的 AI 能达到 Epoch 人类员工所需质量的 65%。
首先，这些分数可能反映的是在较容易的评分条目上的成功。例如，AI 能生成有前景的研究方向，但在创建可执行实验这一更难的任务上却举步维艰。在进行一项试点实验时，GPT-6 Astra 为其评估的模型设置的 token 预算过低，导致 22% 的运行无法返回任何答案。但它随后将这些失败视为关于模型能力的关键发现，而非设置缺陷。
总体而言，AI 在定义明确的任务（如编码和数据分析）上表现更好，在开放式任务（如从示例中归纳模式以及涉及判断的任务）上表现更差。当被要求设计一张图形并提供许多 Epoch 风格的示例时，Fable 5.1 生成了一张杂乱无章的图表，塞满了过多信息，无法有效传达。相比之下，接受同一任务的 Epoch 设计师提供了一张简洁清晰的图表。
这些发现为经济影响为何滞后提供了一种可能的解释——65% 还不够。如果人类提交了这些任务中的任何一个，都会被拒绝或修改。虽然这样的产出可能有帮助，但仍需要人类来评估并修正每一个错误。但随着 AI 不断进步，它将在更多任务上越过 100% 的门槛，届时人类就会把该任务交给 AI。
在这项评估中，已经有一个任务出现了这种情况。我们移除了一个基础的图表生成任务，因为 Fable 5.1 大多数时候能在一次尝试中生成可接受的图表。Epoch 现在已在我们日常工作中部分自动化了这一步骤。随着 AI 在更多任务上达到人类质量阈值，我们预计会看到更多的经济影响。
来源： Epoch AI：Gradient Updates · epochai.substack.com

items.excerpt:
Lean Solutions Group finds that 69% of organizations have moved beyond isolated AI use cases, yet only 19% have redesigned workflows.
Enterprises are adopting artificial intelligence much faster than they are redesigning operations to realize AI’s full business value, according to an Everest Group research report released by Lean Solutions Group.
The research finds that 69% of organizations have moved beyond isolated AI use cases, yet only 19% have significantly or extensively redesigned workflows to support collaboration between people in the form of experts in the loop and AI. Just 15% report comparable redesign of workforce roles.
The report, “Designing the Human + AI Enterprise: A Transformation Agenda for Supply Chain-Intensive Industries,” is based on a survey of more than 200 U.S.-focused senior decisionmakers in transportation, logistics, and other supply chain-intensive industries.
“The challenge is no longer simply getting AI into the business. It is changing how work gets done,” said Jack Freker, CEO of Lean Solutions Group. “Technology can analyze, recommend, and automate at scale, but people remain accountable for the outcome. The organizations that get the most from AI will combine experts in the loop, intelligent technology, and redesigned processes in a way that improves performance for customers.”
“The goal is not maximum AI autonomy,” Freker added. “It is a faster, more reliable path from insight to accountable action. AI should handle work within clearly defined boundaries, while experts provide the judgment and ownership that complex supply chain operations require.”
Looking ahead for leading opportunities for Human + AI transformation in two to three years, survey respondents identified transportation planning and execution (53%), workforce scheduling and labor management (49%), and supply chain planning and coordination (48%).

items.excerpt:
Technology is now conducting tasks in ocean shipping, air freight, and customs brokerage.
Freight broker C.H. Robinson is now using artificial intelligence (AI) agents to perform work in ocean shipping, air freight, and customs brokerage , saying that the new technology brings substantial speed-to-market gains, precision, and agility to customers’ supply chains without sacrificing human oversight or personal attention.
According to the company, the move is significant because it shows an expansion of C.H. Robinson’s “Lean AI” capabilities into freight forwarding, for the benefit of more customers, and into work so complex that a single shipping task can require over a dozen AI agents working in tandem.
The new agents have been assigned to do work including:
“As we’ve brought our AI playbook to global forwarding, the benefits keep compounding,” said Mike Short, President of Global Forwarding. “Customers have information they need sooner. Data is more consistent. Processes are more predictable. When plans change or disruptions occur, customers can more quickly evaluate a new routing, mode of shipping, schedule, or price. The faster we get you a quote and handle your booking, the faster you get the ideal carrier and the ideal sailing or flight.”
For example, C.H. Robinson uses one set of AI agents to manage requests for ocean bookings. They launched in China in August, will roll out to the rest of Asia in Q4, and are expected to be live globally in Q1 2027. One of those AI agents enhances booking requests with customer-specific context, ensuring the other agents operate with maximum efficiency while still taking into account individual customer preferences, requirements and procedures for their shipments.
“We have more work to do automating all the steps for booking, but this is already a major leap forward,” said Mike Neill, C.H. Robinson’s Chief Technology Officer. “Before agentic AI, we’d developed digital booking forms and data exchange setups with customers, but over the course of about 10 years achieved only about 5% automation for ocean and air booking requests. Why was that such a tough hill to climb? Primarily because you quote your customer, then it’s their suppliers booking with you. A customer might have 50 suppliers. With our agentic AI, all those booking requests no longer need to be handled manually.”

items.excerpt:
Systems will operate using self-driving technology from Aurora.
The Ontario, Canada-based truck transportation provider Charger Logistics intends to purchase up to 500 autonomous trucks controlled by technology from self-driving platform provider Aurora, the companies said today.
The agreement builds upon Charger’s existing contract with Aurora signed in July, underscoring the carrier’s belief that the technology—called the Aurora Driver—will be critical to expanding its network and strengthening its business.
Charger operates across the U.S. and Mexico, moving goods for the food and beverage, pharmaceutical, automotive, and retail industries. Under the non-binding memorandum of understanding (MOU), the carrier would purchase 500 Aurora Driver-powered trucks, with delivery taking place over 2027 and 2028. Charger plans to deploy the trucks on current and new high-volume routes near the border and throughout the country.
Upon the final agreement, Charger intends to subscribe to Aurora’s Driver as a Service (DaaS) model, where ownership over the physical asset allows them to maximize Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) savings. In parallel, Aurora benefits from an expected high-margin, capital-efficient, and asset-light business. DaaS agreements are a critical component to Aurora’s plan to scale to 200 driverless trucks by the end of 2026 and to 30,000 driverless trucks by 2030.
“Since launching autonomous operations along the Laredo corridor, we’ve realized immediate operational benefits that point to a clear path to scaling,” said Andy Khera, President of Charger Logistics. “Aurora’s plans to open long-haul, high-volume routes position us to scale geographically while we integrate autonomy from our TMS to the road, building a resilient and autonomous ecosystem for our customers."

items.excerpt:
webframe is a neat little project from Jeff Lindsay which lets you "run a web page like a program" - you point it at a URL or file and it executes it in a hidden headless web view and outputs console.log() to standard output and any exceptions to standard error.
It's written in Go on top of the glaze library, which provides access to a system browser ("WKWebView on macOS, WebKitGTK on Linux, WebView2 on Windows") so it doesn't need to bundle its own browser engine.
It reminds me of my own shot-scraper javascript tool, albeit in a much smaller package that doesn't depend on Playwright.
I had Claude Opus 5.5 put it through its paces and prepare a research report for me. Here's the prompt I used:
Explore https://github.com/tractordev/webframe try running it and put it though its paces, build a few exploratory prototypes, then evaluate it as a potential sandboxing tool and as a tool for scraping web pages using the same patterns encouraged by the "shot-scraper JavaScript" command (see simonw/shot-scraper on GitHub, docs directory)

items.title: Let Chaos Reign, and Then Rein In Chaos
items.description: Replit and the Agent Habitat
items.excerpt:
Replit for Business launched today! To hear more from Amjad Masad, CEO of Replit, see his post here on the rise of the self-driving company.
One thing I love about Amjad is, sometimes he really says the thing and articulates something that other people weren’t brave enough or clear enough in their thinking to express. He has one of those today, as part of Replit’s idea of an Agent Habitat as the way that more businesses are going to become self-driving companies. What Amjad says that’s so on the money is one great word: chaos . “Today, most agents live somewhere chaotic. They run in chat windows, personal accounts, and one-off scripts, holding whatever credentials and data someone handed them. Nobody decided what they could touch, and nobody can see what they did.”
Chaos! It’s one of the most underrated concepts in disruptive technology adoption. One of the best tells that a technology will actually change the world is, “Does it make a chaotic entrance?” And then the most important question thereafter, as Andy Grove put it, is, who is going to let chaos reign, and then rein in the chaos?
Throughout the history of computers and the internet, the most interesting, disruptive and ultimately consequential technologies are the ones that enter workplaces in a chaotic sort of way. What Replit really gets is that this joyful chaos can’t be extinguished: it has to be reined in just the right amount, so that all of the bottoms-up enthusiasm and ownership stays alive within an optimal habitat. Because the same excitement and ambition driving the initial chaos is also what’s creating deep organizational alignment, from the bottom up inside businesses, that makes these companies come alive.
Agents are joining a long tradition of technologies that started as chaos and got reined in just the right amount:

items.title: Our newest AI Quest: Mapping the human brain
items.description: Learn AI literacy via Google’s latest AI Quests lesson on neuroscience, “Polar Peaks.”
items.excerpt:
Our third lesson in our AI Quests series, “Polar Peaks,” teaches students key AI literacy skills while delving into neuroscience.
Your browser does not support the audio element.
Google Research and the Stanford Accelerator for Learning just launched "Polar Peaks," an interactive quest that teaches students ages 11 to 14 how to map the human brain using artificial intelligence. This program helps students practice data cleaning and model testing while emphasizing the need for human oversight in technology. You can access new teacher training modules through the Google AI Educator Series to help bring these lessons into your classroom.
Google launched a new game called "Polar Peaks" that lets you act like a scientist to map the human brain using AI. You’ll learn how to solve real-world problems while discovering how to use AI responsibly. It’s a fun way to see how researchers use technology to make big scientific breakthroughs. Teachers even get special training to help you explore these challenges in class.
Today, we’re launching “Polar Peaks”, our third quest in the AI Quests series, created by Google Research and the Stanford Accelerator for Learning to teach students how AI works and how to use it responsibly. AI Quests invites students ages 11 to 14 to step into the shoes of Google researchers to tackle some of humanity’s biggest challenges.
More than 400,000 quests have been completed to date, localized to 10 languages. Alongside the new quest, we’re also releasing training modules for teachers.
In the first two quests, students tackle flood forecasting and eye disease detection, inspired by Google Research’s Flood Forecasting initiative and AI model for diabetic retinopathy screening. Our newest quest, “Polar Peaks,” has students travel to the frontiers of neuroscience and see how AI can speed up scientific research.
With the guidance of in-game mentors, students scan and map the neurons in the brain to better understand the game character’s memory loss. They complete tasks like data cleaning and model testing, learning firsthand that AI requires careful human oversight and critical thinking.
The quest is inspired by over a decade of our research in connectomics: the science of mapping neural networks in the brain. Upon completion of the quest, students hear from two researchers behind our real-world breakthroughs, including the recent mapping of the complete fruit fly brain, the largest brain map by number of neurons to date.

items.excerpt:
Apple Creator Studio adds powerful new AI features and even more creative tools
Apple 为 Creator Studio 推出更新，Final Cut Pro for Mac 内置 MotionVFX 视觉效果库并接入含视频素材的 Content Hub。
官方新闻稿列出 Final Cut Pro、Logic Pro 与 Keynote 等应用的 AI 能力变化，读者可据此评估对创作工作流的影响。
此次更新为 Final Cut Pro 带来内置 MotionVFX 内容、Content Hub 中的视频素材、Logic Pro 扩展的音乐创作工具，以及 Logic Pro、Keynote、Pages 和 Numbers 的全新智能功能
Apple Creator Studio 迎来变革性更新，包括 Final Cut Pro 的内置 MotionVFX 内容、Content Hub 中的视频素材、Logic Pro 扩展的音乐创作工具，以及 Logic Pro、Keynote、Pages 和 Numbers 的全新智能功能。
加利福尼亚州库比蒂诺 Apple 今日为 Apple Creator Studio 推出变革性更新。Apple Creator Studio 是一套强大的创意应用集合，旨在将工作室级工具交到 Mac、iPad 和 iPhone 上的现代创作者手中。Mac 版 Final Cut Pro 现内置 MotionVFX——一个包含视觉特效、插件、转场、模板和动态图形工具的丰富集合——并支持在 Pixelmator Pro 中无缝编辑。Apple 精选的 Content Hub 现已包含视频素材，并已在 Final Cut Pro 中提供。使用 Mac 版 Logic Pro 的音乐创作者将获得一个测试版的全新智能助手， 1 一个增强的 Stem Splitter（现可分离鼓声），以及一个重新设计的浏览器，它整合了所有声音，具备音乐理解能力，甚至包含一个 Splice 库。Pixelmator Pro 推出 Generate Fill，让创作者可以使用自然语言转换图像的选定区域。Keynote、Pages 和 Numbers 推出测试版的全新 AI 功能，包括能够理解文档上下文的助手 2 ，以及用于工作流自动化的全新 Model Context Protocol (MCP) 支持。 3 它们还在 Content Hub 中新增了库存视频，以及新的高级主题和模板。
Apple Creator Studio 更新将于今年 11 月在 App Store 上架，现有订阅用户可免费更新。 4
“这是自 Apple Creator Studio 推出以来我们最激动人心的一次更新。Final Cut Pro 中的 MotionVFX 内容让订阅用户能够快速获取大量专业视频特效和内容，为整套产品带来巨大价值，”Apple 全球产品营销高级总监（负责应用与 iCloud）Brent Chiu-Watson 表示。“Logic Pro 的全新浏览器让用户在创作音乐时能够探索和尝试比以往更多的声音。Pixelmator Pro 先进的填充功能现在让用户能够完全重新构想图像的任意部分。而 Logic Pro、Keynote、Pages 和 Numbers 中的助手功能将彻底改变人们与这些应用互动并学习使用它们的方式。”
Final Cut Pro 为 Mac 和 iPad 带来了一组卓越的全新功能，面向视频剪辑师、内容创作者和电影制作人，从初出茅庐的故事讲述者到深陷复杂剪辑的资深专业人士皆可受益。Final Cut Pro for Mac 现将 MotionVFX 直接集成到应用中，让剪辑师可以访问数千种元素，包括具有独特主题的模板、时尚的图形、标题和转场，以及用于 rotoscoping、跟踪和调色的工具。剪辑师还可以直接在 Final Cut Pro 内访问 Content Hub，获取 Apple 精选的素材视频、照片和背景库，以填补空缺、增添精致感或激发新想法，而无需离开工作流程。

跨应用工作流程和视觉创作在 Final Cut Pro 中也实现了重大飞跃。剪辑师可以直接在 Pixelmator Pro 中打开时间线上的任何图像，利用高级编辑工具，并将更改自动保存回项目——无需重新导入。借助高级图像生成功能，用户可以直接在项目中根据文本描述创建令人惊叹的图像、应用快速编辑并调整视觉风格。Final Cut Pro 还引入了强大的工作流程改进，包括更多关键帧缓动选项以实现更精细的动画控制、能够将片段与主故事线断开以将其放置在时间线上的任何位置，以及 23 种新的转录语言，使添加字幕和搜索素材比以往任何时候都更容易。

items.title: Liquid AI 发布 LFM3 多模态开源权重模型家族，2B 级覆盖文本、视觉、音频、omni 和决策模型
items.description: Liquid AI 发布新一代 LFM3 模型家族，以 LFM3-1.7B-Base 为共享骨干，首批开放六个 2B 级模型（文本、视觉、音频、omni 及两个决策模型）的开放权重，可在 Hugging Face、Playground 和 Liquid AI API 获取。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/vx4t4ldzajj3lhb8luhg9dy9s
items.excerpt:
Introducing LFM3: Every Modality for Specialized Intelligence
Liquid AI 发布新一代 LFM3 模型家族，以 LFM3-1.7B-Base 为共享骨干，首批开放六个 2B 级模型（文本、视觉、音频、omni 及两个决策模型）的开放权重，可在 Hugging Face、Playground 和 Liquid AI API 获取。
原文给出 LFM3 各模型的具体架构、基准和端侧性能数据，读者可以据此评估小参数量多模态模型在本地方案中的可行性。
今天，我们很高兴地宣布 LFM3 ，这是我们新一代的 Liquid Foundation Models（LFMs），专为专业化智能而打造。LFM3 模型家族天生多模态，将文本、视觉、音频、全模态和决策模型统一到一个全新的共享骨干网络上。LFM3 家族的首个版本覆盖 2B 参数级别的模型。
LFM3 基于全新的混合架构和 22T token 的预训练构建，在保持高效的同时，表达能力远超 LFM2 。小巧快速模型中的额外容量，使 LFM3 成为同类中面向专业化智能的理想起点：它可以在本地微调，可以在任何设备上运行，并且能力足以成为特定任务上可靠的专家。
基础模型和后训练模型均为开放权重，现已在 Hugging Face 、 我们的 Playground 和 Liquid AI API 上提供。请查看我们的 文档 ，了解如何在本地运行和微调它们。
LFM3 实例是专业化智能的理想候选。用你自己的数据微调它们，并将它们部署到你的应用运行之处。享受这篇文章吧。
下载权重 在 Liquid API 中试用 在 Playground 中试用 在 Pipette 中跑基准测试
LFM2 表明，短卷积与注意力的混合架构可以在设备端快速运行，同时不牺牲质量。其设计源自我们的 自动化硬件在环架构搜索 。对于 LFM3，我们利用这一搜索为该架构针对智能体用例重新设计，这类用例需要更高的每参数能力，以及在长上下文上的快速推理。
我们还扩展了硬件在环的范围：LFM2 时仅涉及一部手机和一台笔记本的 CPU，而 LFM3 覆盖 14 种设备与后端组合：手机（Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra 和 OnePlus 15）、Raspberry Pi 5、笔记本（Apple M4 Max 和 AMD Ryzen AI）、Arm 和 x86 云 CPU，以及 GPU 和高通 Hexagon NPU。
门控短卷积仍占一半以上的层。为了在不拖慢长上下文的前提下增加能力，我们尝试将其中一些替换为其他序列模块，滑动窗口注意力（SWA）给出了最佳的质量与速度权衡。下文描述的其他改动，我们只在它们能提升质量且不带来明显速度损失时才保留。收益在长上下文上显现：按参数计，LFM3-1.7B 在边缘设备上的短提示上与 LFM2-1.2B 相当，而在上下文达到 8K token 时约快 25%。
三混合层组合。 LFM3 结合了三种算子：门控短卷积、滑动窗口注意力（SWA）和全局注意力。在其 24 层中，13 层为卷积，5 层为窗口大小为 256 个 token 的 SWA，6 层为全局注意力。卷积的核大小也从 LFM2 的 3 提升到了 7。
逐头门控注意力。 一个 sigmoid 门控会缩放每个头的输出，因此当某个头没有可补充的信息时，它可以被关闭。这有助于 抑制损害量化的激活离群值 并 提升训练稳定性 。
部分 RoPE。 全局注意力层只对每个头中频率最高的那一半进行旋转，低频那一半保持不旋转，因此这些维度 无论距离远近都能在内容上匹配 。SWA 层保留完整的 RoPE。
LFM3 使用与 LFM2.5-8B-A1B 相同的 128K 词表，该词表旨在更高效地对非拉丁文字进行分词。
训练。 LFM3-1.7B-Base 在 22T token 上进行了预训练。与 LFM2 相比，其数据组合增加了更多科学论文、仓库级代码、更广泛的知识来源，以及相当多的数学内容。最后 3.5T token 是在精选的高质量数据上进行的中期训练阶段，其中包含更大比例的智能体轨迹和多样化的工具调用，为模型的智能体后训练做准备。该阶段还将上下文窗口扩展到了 256K token。
LFM3 的首个版本包含六个模型，全部从同一个 LFM3-1.7B-Base 主干分支而来，参数量都在 2B 左右。其中四个覆盖不同的输入模态（文本、视觉、音频和全模态），最后两个是从视觉模型和全模态模型专门化而来的决策模型。你无需运行一个大型通用模型，而是可以选择适合自身用例的模型，对其进行定制，并在设备端运行。
LFM3-1.7B 是一款面向本地智能体和专用应用的文本模型，具有 256K token 的上下文窗口。
它经过后训练，可在 Hermes Agent、Pi 和 OpenClaw 等智能体框架中运行。它可以分拣你的收件箱、管理你的日历、在网上研究主题、通过 WhatsApp 向你发送晨间简报，并使用工具搜索在数千个选项中找出合适的工具。由于 token 是免费的，数十个智能体可以在后台持续运行。你只需在单块 GPU 上进行一次简短的微调，就能让它适配你的领域、框架和工具。
在智能体任务上，LFM3-1.7B 可与数倍于其规模的模型竞争。它在指令遵循以及 BFCL 和 ToolSandbox 上的函数调用方面领先，并在浏览器和业务应用中的长任务（WebArena-Verified、AutomationBench）上击败 Qwen3.5-9B。更大的模型在智能体编程和知识方面仍然胜出，因为规模在这些方面最为重要，但搜索有助于缩小知识差距，使其在 Humanity's Last Exam 上的得分几乎翻倍。
在设备端，我们使用 llama.cpp 在 Q4_0 和 32K token 上下文下测量指标。LFM3-1.7B 在三台设备上都是最快的模型，解码速度比第二名快 1.8 到

items.title: Apple 发布搭载 M6 芯片的 14 英寸 MacBook Pro，起售价 $1,999
items.description: Apple 发布搭载全新 M6 芯片的 14 英寸 MacBook Pro，配备 12 核 CPU 和 12 核 GPU，相比 M5 图形性能最高快 30%、端侧 AI 工作负载最高快 25%，电池续航最长 24 小时。新机支持 Wi-Fi 7 和蓝牙 6，可本地运行 LLM，10 月 28 日开启预购、11 月 6 日发售，起售价 $1,999（教育优惠 $1,899）。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/o0okltd585bcx5lh6bkq53n59
items.excerpt:
Apple introduces the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6
Apple 发布搭载全新 M6 芯片的 14 英寸 MacBook Pro，配备 12 核 CPU 和 12 核 GPU，相比 M5 图形性能最高快 30%、端侧 AI 工作负载最高快 25%，电池续航最长 24 小时。新机支持 Wi-Fi 7 和蓝牙 6，可本地运行 LLM，10 月 28 日开启预购、11 月 6 日发售，起售价 $1,999（教育优惠 $1,899）。
官方发布稿给出 M6 相对 M5 和 M1 的具体性能数字、端侧 AI 能力与售价，读者可据此评估是否值得升级。
14英寸MacBook Pro搭载M6芯片，性能强劲，具备新一代AI能力，连接性增强，电池续航最长可达24小时，带来更高价值
14英寸MacBook Pro搭载全新M6芯片，带来卓越性能、AI能力和最长可达24小时的电池续航——使其价值更具吸引力。
加利福尼亚州库比蒂诺 Apple今日宣布推出全新的 搭载M6的14英寸MacBook Pro ，为大学生、商务用户、创作者等带来更强劲的性能、强大的端侧AI能力和更快的连接性。M6配备先进的12核CPU，拥有全球最快的CPU核心，因此从生产力任务到要求更高的专业工作流程，一切都感觉极其快速和响应灵敏。 1 与M5相比，12核GPU的图形性能提升最高可达30%，AI工作负载速度提升最高可达25%，使搭载M6的14英寸MacBook Pro成为需要强大性能的用户的超值之选。 2 对于从M1升级的用户，性能提升更为显著，图形性能最高提升可达11倍，AI性能最高提升可达13倍。 3 凭借GPU中额外的神经加速器和双16核神经网络引擎，M6将MacBook Pro打造成更强大的AI平台——从在各应用和macOS中利用Siri AI和Apple Intelligence功能，到在本地运行LLM，同时保护用户隐私。 4 此外，14英寸MacBook Pro支持Wi-Fi 7和蓝牙6，超快存储让处理大文件、导出项目和运行高要求的AI工作流程飞速完成。凭借最长可达24小时的出色电池续航，无论插电还是使用电池，它都能提供同样卓越的性能，让用户随时随地工作、创作和追求热爱。 3 它还提供用户喜爱的先进功能，包括配备纳米纹理选项的惊艳Liquid Retina XDR显示屏、12MP Center Stage摄像头、沉浸式六扬声器音响系统和丰富的端口。结合macOS 27，全新的搭载M6的14英寸MacBook Pro对现有Mac用户和首次接触Mac的用户而言都是一次重大升级。提供深空黑色和银色两种配色，明天10月28日起可预订，11月6日星期五开始发售。
全新的搭载M6的14英寸MacBook Pro将新一代性能和强大的端侧AI融入便携设计，助力学生、创意工作者、开发者和商务专业人士随时随地开展工作。
“14 英寸 MacBook Pro 是广大用户首选的专业级笔记本电脑——从大学生，到各行各业的商务专业人士，再到在一台设备上完成所有工作的多领域创作者，”Apple 硬件工程副总裁 Shelly Goldberg 表示。“凭借强大的 M6 芯片，我们将性能提升到新的水平，CPU 速度和图形性能均有提升，端侧 AI 能力也更加强大。凭借出色的电池续航、卓越的 Liquid Retina XDR 显示屏以及更快的连接能力，搭载 M6 的新款 14 英寸 MacBook Pro 在性能、能力和价值方面实现了绝佳组合。”

items.excerpt:
Plastic totes, pallets, and containers are becoming intelligent conveyors of information throughout the supply chain—from point A to point B and back again.
Victoria Kickham, Senior Editor , started her career as a newspaper reporter in the Boston area before moving into B2B journalism. She has covered manufacturing, distribution, and supply chain issues for a variety of publications in the industrial and electronics sectors, and now writes about warehousing, transportation, and logistics trends for DC VELOCITY . Victoria earned a bachelor’s degree in English from the University of New Hampshire and a master’s degree in English from Northeastern University.
Recent research predicts a shift in the asset-tracking technology market, which has been a game-changer in logistics for its ability to provide visibility into transportation and freight movement. Vehicle-tracking devices have been the primary drivers of market growth, but analysts at global research firm Counterpoint Research are predicting a different scenario by 2032, when they say the majority of those gains will come from devices aimed at other applications—particularly those that provide a lens into a shipment’s entire supply chain journey, from origin through distribution to the retailer and everywhere in between.
The trend reflects growing demand to track and monitor just about everything that moves into, around, and out of a warehouse or distribution center—right down to the containers and packaging used to ship small orders in addition to bulk items. Reusable packaging, in particular, is predicted to be one of the newest drivers of this market shift.
“For years, the asset-tracking market has been largely driven by vehicle telematics, with fleet management and logistics accounting for the majority of deployments,” the Counterpoint researchers wrote in a July report. “However, the market is entering a new phase as enterprises shift their focus from tracking vehicles to tracking individual assets, industrial equipment, and inventory, along with newer categories such as reusable packaging and livestock. This transition is being driven by the need for real-time visibility that now extends beyond the vehicle to the assets it carries.”

items.title: Anthropic’s IPO Reveals a $430 Billion AI Supply Chain Bet
items.description: Artificial intelligence has a capacity-planning problem. Not an abstract one involving algorithms, but a familiar industrial problem: how much capacity to contract years in advance, how to finance it, and what happens when demand or technology changes before those commitments expire. Anthropic’s October 26 public filing for an initial public offering provides an unusually clear […] The post Anthropic’s IPO Reveals a $430 Billion AI Supply Chain Bet appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Artificial intelligence has a capacity-planning problem. Not an abstract one involving algorithms, but a familiar industrial problem: how much capacity to contract years in advance, how to finance it, and what happens when demand or technology changes before those commitments expire.
Anthropic’s October 26 public filing for an initial public offering provides an unusually clear view of this challenge. The developer of Claude plans to list on Nasdaq under the symbol ANT, although its offering price and share count remain undecided. The company reported $16.3 billion in revenue during the first half of 2026, roughly fourteen times the comparable 2025 figure. Its $80.7 billion reported net loss is dramatic, but largely reflects noncash revaluations of financing instruments; the operating loss was approximately $693 million.
For supply chain executives, the more consequential disclosure concerns commitments to computing infrastructure. Yahoo Finance calculated that four major agreements involving Broadcom, Google, Amazon, and Microsoft represent approximately $430 billion in long-term equipment-lease and cloud commitments. The underlying contracts differ, and the figure is not an amount due immediately. Other announced arrangements could increase Anthropic’s access to computing capacity considerably, but their terms should not all be treated as equally binding.
Here is the underlying business question: Is Anthropic buying supply assurance at a scale justified by future demand, or locking itself into infrastructure that could become economically obsolete faster than expected?
Manufacturers commit to materials, factory capacity, and transportation contracts ahead of demand because inadequate supply can be more expensive than carrying excess. Anthropic is doing something comparable with computing. The scarce inputs are high-performance chips, servers, networking, available data-center space, and electricity. Reserving them makes it possible to serve customers when demand surges.
The analogy goes further. Computing capacity has inventory-like economics, but there is an important difference. An unused component might be held for a future production run. An unused hour of computing service cannot be recovered. Worse, the economic usefulness of today’s computing hardware can decline rapidly as newer processors and more efficient AI models change the cost per unit of work.

items.title: From Intelligence to Execution: Join Us at the 2027 ARC Industry Leadership Forum
items.description: Artificial intelligence is rapidly changing what supply chain and industrial organizations can see, predict, and decide. The next challenge is more consequential: turning that intelligence into action. A transportation system can identify an impending delivery failure. A planning application can recommend a better allocation of inventory. A warehouse can anticipate tomorrow’s capacity constraints. But recognizing […] The post From Intelligence to Execution: Join Us at the 2027 ARC Industry Leadership Forum appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Artificial intelligence is rapidly changing what supply chain and industrial organizations can see, predict, and decide. The next challenge is more consequential: turning that intelligence into action.
A transportation system can identify an impending delivery failure. A planning application can recommend a better allocation of inventory. A warehouse can anticipate tomorrow’s capacity constraints. But recognizing an opportunity or a problem is only the beginning. The real value comes when organizations can translate those insights into coordinated, reliable execution.
That is why we’re particularly excited about the 31st Annual ARC Industry Leadership Forum , taking place February 22–25, 2027, in Orlando, Florida.
This year’s theme, “From Intelligence to Execution: Scaling AI Across Industrial Operations and Supply Chain,” addresses one of the defining challenges facing our industry. How do we move beyond promising pilots, disconnected applications, and impressive demonstrations to build operations that are genuinely more intelligent, responsive, and resilient?
At Logistics Viewpoints, these are questions we explore every day. As part of ARC Advisory Group, we have the opportunity to bring those conversations together with the manufacturers, supply chain executives, technology innovators, and industry experts who are putting these ideas into practice.
Supply chain technology has entered a particularly interesting period. AI is being incorporated into transportation management, warehouse operations, supply chain planning, manufacturing execution, and asset management. Robotics and autonomous systems are becoming more capable, while the boundaries between digital intelligence and physical operations continue to evolve.
Yet the technologies themselves are only part of the story.
An AI recommendation that never reaches the people or systems responsible for execution has limited operational value. The same is true of autonomous systems that cannot communicate effectively with adjacent processes, or planning applications that optimize decisions without accounting for conditions on the factory floor or in the distribution network.
The organizations that distinguish themselves in the coming years will be those capable of connecting intelligence with execution across traditional functional and technology boundaries.
The 2027 ARC Forum is designed to examine precisely how that transition is taking place.

items.title: When Visibility Becomes Noise: Why Exception Context Matters More Than Event Volume
items.description: When Visibility Becomes Noise: Why Exception Context Matters More Than Event Volume sounds counterintuitive because visibility has been one of the central supply-chain technology goals for years. But as event volume rises, the limiting factor can shift from seeing too little to processing too much. The post When Visibility Becomes Noise: Why Exception Context Matters More Than Event Volume appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Supply-chain visibility can become counterproductive when event volume grows faster than the organization’s ability to interpret and act. As signals multiply, the limiting factor can shift from seeing too little to processing too much, increasing cognitive load and slowing the response that visibility was meant to improve.
Telematics, carrier feeds, IoT, warehouse events, weather, risk data, and partner networks can expose thousands of state changes. Humans cannot investigate all of them with equal depth. Thresholds alone are a weak filter because the same deviation can be harmless in one context and critical in another. This is the failure mode implied by The New Economics of Logistics Visibility : event abundance can consume decision capacity unless the architecture filters for consequence and connects only meaningful signals to action.
A decision-and-action capability that detects meaningful exceptions, assembles operational context, evaluates consequence, recommends or executes a response within guardrails, and monitors whether the intervention worked. The system needs to understand the object affected, the downstream dependency, the customer or service commitment, the time to intervene, and the available alternatives. That context turns event volume into a prioritized operating queue.
Every unnecessary alert consumes attention, creates switching cost, and teaches users to distrust the system. Important exceptions can become buried inside routine deviations. The economic effect appears as slower decisions, planner overload, missed intervention windows, and growing exception backlog.
The mature design suppresses non-consequential events, groups related signals, explains why an exception matters, and prepares the next useful action. It should also learn from overrides and outcomes so qualification improves over time. The goal is not maximum transparency; it is decision-relevant observability.

items.title: Holiday Shopping Affected by Affordability
items.description: National Retail Federation survey says 56% of holiday shoppers say the state of the economy will affect their holiday spending plans.
items.excerpt:
Shopping habits are changing due to the issue of affordability. More than half of holiday shoppers (56%) say the state of the economy will affect their holiday spending plans this year, according to the National Retail Federation’s annual consumer survey conducted by Prosper Insights & Analytics.
Among those consumers, 43% plan to shop for sales more often, 31% will comparison shop online more often and 29% will use coupons more often, among other strategies to make the season more affordable.
“With affordability top of mind, holiday shoppers are taking a thoughtful approach to spending, balancing value with preserving traditions that make the holiday season special,” NRF Vice President of Industry and Consumer Insights Allison Zeller said in a statement.
“Retailers understand consumer budget priorities and are responding with compelling products, promotions and shopping experiences that make it easier to find value while still capturing the holiday excitement.”
Consistent with recent years, nearly all U.S. adults (91%) plan to celebrate winter holidays including Christmas, Hanukkah or Kwanzaa.
Forty-three percent of holiday shoppers plan to begin browsing and buying for the holiday season before November, in line with 42% last year.
Among those starting early, 50% do so to spread out their holiday shopping budgets, while 37% say the prices and promotions are too good to pass up.
Affordability is also top of mind for those waiting until November to start their shopping, with 46% of these shoppers saying they plan to wait until November and December because it is when they find the best prices and promotions.
While many consumers begin their holiday shopping early, many hold off on making the bulk of their purchases until later in the season, with sales and promotions continuing to play an important role throughout the holiday season. Nearly two-thirds (64%) of consumers say they are likely to wait until Thanksgiving weekend to do most of their shopping, in line with 63% last year.
“From getting an early start to waiting for major deals and promotions, consumers are choosing when to shop based on what works best for them,” Prosper Executive Vice President of Strategy Phil Ris t said. “Even with a significant portion of shoppers beginning before November, many still plan to take advantage of deals and promotions during Thanksgiving weekend to make progress on their holiday shopping.”
